# domestic-ui

> domestic-ui is a design system built on native HTML, CSS custom properties and cascade layers. Link one stylesheet and plain semantic HTML gets its look in light and dark, with WCAG 2.2 AA as the accessibility baseline; theme it by overriding semantic tokens. It packages existing web standards and well-known patterns: nothing here is original.

To use it, link `css/domestic.css` (copy the `css/` folder or clone https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui). Plain semantic HTML then gets the full look with no classes. Each component exposes one `data-<component>` attribute whose value is space-separated words matched with `~=`, such as `data-button="primary small"`, never classes; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA (`disabled`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-busy`, `aria-invalid`). Layout primitives and utilities are classes (`.cluster`, `.grid`, `.scroll`, `.stack`, `.visually-hidden`), tuned with custom properties. Theme only by overriding semantic `--dui-*` tokens; primitive tokens are internal and may change.

## domestic-ui

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.html

domestic-ui is a design system built on native HTML, CSS custom properties and cascade layers. Link one stylesheet and plain semantic HTML gets its look in light and dark, with WCAG 2.2 AA as the accessibility baseline; theme it by overriding semantic tokens. It packages existing web standards and well-known patterns: nothing here is original.

### Install and use

domestic-ui is plain CSS with no build step. Copy the `css/` folder into your project, or clone the repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui.git
```

Link the single entry point. Plain semantic HTML then gets the full look; base elements need no classes.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/domestic.css">
```

Its imports use relative paths, so it works from file paths and from subpaths. File paths under `css/` are public API; see [Agent-friendly by design](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/agent-friendly-by-design.md).

### Layer order

`css/domestic.css` declares the [cascade layers](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/cascade-layers.md) once, lowest priority first. Later layers win regardless of selector specificity, and your own unlayered CSS beats all of them.

```css
@layer reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities;
```

### Theming

Override semantic `--dui-*` tokens on `:root`, or on an element with `data-theme` to scope a theme ([Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.md), [theming example](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/theming.html)).
Force a color scheme on the page or any subtree with `data-color-scheme="light"` or `data-color-scheme="dark"`.

### Component API

Each component exposes one `data-<component>` attribute. Its value is a list of space-separated words matched with the [`~=` attribute selector](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Attribute_selectors), like [`rel`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/rel): `data-button="primary small"`. Component APIs use no classes. State is carried by native attributes and ARIA: `disabled`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-busy`, `aria-invalid`.

**Our choice:** One attribute is one API to learn, it reads as a sentence (`data-button="primary small"`), and it cannot pile up like modifier classes.

Layout primitives and utilities from M1 are classes: `.cluster`, `.grid`, `.scroll`, `.stack`, `.visually-hidden`. Base elements need no API: write semantic HTML.

## Principles

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/index.html

domestic-ui packages existing web standards and well-known patterns. Nothing here is
original: the rules below come from the [WHATWG HTML Living Standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/),
the [W3C CSS specifications](https://www.w3.org/Style/CSS/specs.en.html),
[WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), the
[ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) and
[MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/). Where we had to pick between valid
options, the pick is labeled **Our choice:** with one line saying why.

### Sections

1. [Native element first](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/native-element-first.md)
2. [Agent-friendly by design](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/agent-friendly-by-design.md)
3. [Accessibility baseline: WCAG 2.2 AA](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)
4. [Cascade layers](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/cascade-layers.md)
5. [Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.md)
6. [Opinions we hold](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/opinions-we-hold.md)
7. [Layout primitives](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/layout-primitives.md)
8. [Web components](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/web-components.md)
9. [Explainers](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/explainers.md)
10. [Tooling](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/tooling.md)

## Native element first

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/native-element-first.html

- Use the HTML element that already has the semantics and behavior you need:
  `<button>`, `<a href>`, `<dialog>`, `<details>`, `<label>`, `<fieldset>`, `<table>`.
  This is the [first rule of ARIA use](https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1) in W3C *Using ARIA*.
- Add ARIA only when native HTML cannot express something, and only in the ways
  [ARIA in HTML](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/) allows. Never add a role an element
  already has (see the [document conformance rules](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#docconformance)).
- When an interactive widget has no native element, follow its
  [APG pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/) exactly.
- Native behavior beats script: open a `<dialog>` with
  [`showModal()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal)
  or [invoker commands](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API)
  so the browser handles focus, <kbd>Esc</kbd> and inertness.

## Agent-friendly by design

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/agent-friendly-by-design.html

Humans and coding agents should be able to write a whole view from this document alone.

- **Predictable markup.** Plain semantic HTML gets the full look. No wrapper `div`s or
  classes are needed for base elements.
- **One API per thing.** Each layout primitive, utility or component has one documented
  class or attribute, tuned with custom properties, never with modifier classes.
  The API is written in a comment at the top of its CSS file.
- **Paths are API.** `css/domestic.css` and every file under `css/` keep their paths.
  Renaming or moving a file is a breaking change.
- **No hidden JS behavior.** CSS never depends on script. Any script an example uses is
  inline, short, and commented, or one of the documented [web components](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/README.md).
- **Our choice:** class and attribute APIs over custom elements, because they work with
  any templating language and need no JavaScript. Custom elements are used only for behavior
  HTML cannot do, and enhance markup that already works without them.

## Accessibility baseline: WCAG 2.2 AA

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.html

Every example must pass, and every token pair is tested against, these criteria:

| Topic | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text contrast | 4.5:1 for body text, in light **and** dark | [1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html) |
| Non-text contrast | 3:1 for control boundaries and the focus indicator | [1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html) |
| Links | Links keep their underline; color is never the only cue | [1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html) |
| Focus visible | Every focusable element shows a `:focus-visible` outline | [2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html) |
| Focus not obscured | `scroll-padding` keeps focused elements clear of sticky edges | [2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html) |
| Focus appearance (AAA, optional) | The default 2px solid outline with a 2px offset aims to meet it | [2.4.13 Focus Appearance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html) |
| Target size | Controls are at least 44px tall, above the 24px minimum | [2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html) |
| Reduced motion | Duration tokens become `0s` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | [MDN `prefers-reduced-motion`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion), [2.3.3 Animation from Interactions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html) |
| Color scheme | `color-scheme: light dark` plus [`light-dark()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark) in every semantic color | [MDN `color-scheme`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color-scheme) |
| Forced colors | Borders and outlines switch to system colors | [MDN `forced-colors`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors) |

- Never remove an outline without a visible replacement.
- Forms: every control has a `<label>`; groups use `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`
  ([W3C forms tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/)).
- Tables: a `<caption>` and `th` with `scope` ([W3C tables tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/)).
- Images: meaningful `alt` text ([W3C images tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/)).
- Force a scheme on the page or any subtree with `data-color-scheme="light"` or `"dark"`.

## Cascade layers

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/cascade-layers.html

`css/domestic.css` declares the order once, before anything else
([`@layer` on MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@layer),
[CSS Cascade 5](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-cascade-5/#layering)):

```css
@layer reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities;
```

Later layers win over earlier ones regardless of selector specificity, and **your own
unlayered CSS beats all of them**, so overriding never needs `!important` or specificity tricks.

| Layer | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `reset` | A modest reset: `box-sizing`, zero margins, block media, inherited form fonts |
| `tokens` | Primitive and semantic custom properties |
| `base` | Native elements: typography, lists, tables, forms, buttons, dialog, details, focus |
| `layout` | `.stack`, `.cluster`, `.grid`, `[data-scroll]` |
| `components` | Atoms in `css/components/atoms/` (M2) and molecules in `css/components/molecules/` (M3a); organisms later. See the [atoms index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md) and the [molecules index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/README.md) |
| `utilities` | Single-purpose helpers such as `.visually-hidden`; last so they always apply |

**Our choice:** this order, because each layer only refines the ones before it, and a
utility should beat a component the way an inline override would.

## Theming

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.html

### Two tiers of tokens

All tokens are [custom properties](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-variables-1/) on `:root`
with the `--dui-` prefix.

| Tier | File | Named by | Example | Public? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primitive | `css/tokens/primitives.css` | What it is | `--dui-color-blue-600: #3451d1;` `--dui-space-5: 1rem;` | No. Internal, may change in any release. |
| Semantic | `css/tokens/semantic.css` | What it is for | `--dui-color-accent: light-dark(var(--dui-color-blue-600), var(--dui-color-blue-400));` | **Yes.** The stable theming API. |

**Base, layout, utility and component CSS reference only semantic tokens.** They never use
primitives and never hard-code colors or sizes (`0`, `1px` hairlines, percentages, `fr`,
`currentcolor`, `inherit`, `transparent` and system colors are fine). `npm test` enforces
this with `scripts/check-tokens.mjs` (`npm run lint:tokens`), which also rejects literal
colors in `semantic.css`.

**Our choice:** the `--dui-` prefix, so tokens never collide with your own custom properties.

### A theme is a semantic-token override

No build step. Override semantic tokens on `:root` for the whole page, or on any element
with a `data-theme` attribute or a `theme-*` class to scope it:

```css
[data-theme="forest"] {
  --dui-color-surface: light-dark(#f7f5ef, #141a16);
  --dui-color-text: light-dark(#1d2a22, #e4ebe3);
  --dui-color-accent: light-dark(#2f6b3f, #7fcf95);
  --dui-color-accent-contrast: light-dark(#fff, #0f1a13);
}
```

```html
<section data-theme="forest">…</section>
```

[`examples/theming.html`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/theming.html) shows a full scoped theme next to the default.
Check your theme's contrast in both schemes; `tests/tokens.spec.js` shows how.

A few semantic tokens are defined in terms of others (`--dui-color-link`, `--dui-color-focus`
and `--dui-color-accent-hover` follow `--dui-color-accent`; the badge tints
`--dui-color-*-surface` mix a tone into `--dui-color-surface`). A custom property's `var()` is
resolved on the element that declares it ([CSS Variables, "Resolving dependency cycles"](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-variables-1/#cycles)),
so these, plus `color`, `background-color` and `font-family`, are re-applied on every
`[data-theme]`, `.theme-*` and `[data-color-scheme]` element.
**Our choice:** `data-theme` (or a `theme-*` class) as the single scoping API, so one attribute
makes an element a theme root. An override on any other selector (say `.sidebar`) still
reaches properties that read the token directly on an element (borders, buttons, links,
headings, controls), but not inherited text color, background or derived tokens. Add
`data-theme` to that element to get the full effect.

### Semantic tokens (public API)

Renaming or removing a semantic token is a **breaking change**. Primitives are internal and
may change. Fluid `--dui-step-*` values are `clamp()` expressions; see `primitives.css`.

| Token | Purpose | Default (primitive, light / dark) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-color-surface` | Page and control background | light: `color-gray-0` (#fff)<br>dark: `color-gray-900` (#12151b) |
| `--dui-color-surface-raised` | Slightly lifted areas: neutral buttons, zebra rows, cards | light: `color-gray-50` (#f6f7f9)<br>dark: `color-gray-850` (#1b1f27) |
| `--dui-color-surface-sunken` | Recessed areas: code, button hover | light: `color-gray-100` (#eceef2)<br>dark: `color-gray-800` (#252a34) |
| `--dui-color-text` | Body text | light: `color-gray-900` (#12151b)<br>dark: `color-gray-100` (#eceef2) |
| `--dui-color-text-muted` | Secondary text, captions, list markers (still 4.5:1) | light: `color-gray-600` (#545b68)<br>dark: `color-gray-400` (#a3aab6) |
| `--dui-color-border` | Decorative hairlines: tables, hr, details, fieldset | light: `color-gray-200` (#dde0e6)<br>dark: `color-gray-700` (#3a404b) |
| `--dui-color-border-control` | Form control and button boundaries (3:1) | light: `color-gray-500` (#7a8291)<br>dark: `color-gray-500` (#7a8291) |
| `--dui-color-accent` | Brand color: primary button fill, checks, links and focus by default | light: `color-blue-600` (#3451d1)<br>dark: `color-blue-400` (#8ea2ff) |
| `--dui-color-accent-contrast` | Text on accent | light: `color-gray-0` (#fff)<br>dark: `color-gray-900` (#12151b) |
| `--dui-color-link-visited` | Visited links | light: `color-purple-700` (#6b2fb3)<br>dark: `color-purple-300` (#d2a8ff) |
| `--dui-color-danger` | Errors, :user-invalid borders | light: `color-red-700` (#b42318)<br>dark: `color-red-300` (#ff8a80) |
| `--dui-color-success` | Success messages | light: `color-green-700` (#17773a)<br>dark: `color-green-300` (#5fd38d) |
| `--dui-color-warning` | Warning badges and messages | light: `color-amber-700` (#8a5a00)<br>dark: `color-amber-300` (#f2c14e) |
| `--dui-color-info` | Informational alerts and toasts (separate from the accent, so a brand color never reads as a status) | light: `color-blue-700` (#2b43b0)<br>dark: `color-blue-300` (#a8b7ff) |
| `--dui-color-mark` | mark and ::selection background | light: `color-yellow-100` (#fff1a8)<br>dark: `color-yellow-300` (#e3c84f) |
| `--dui-color-mark-text` | Text on mark | light: `color-gray-900` (#12151b)<br>dark: `color-gray-900` (#12151b) |
| `--dui-color-backdrop` | dialog::backdrop | light: `color-black-a40` (rgb(0 0 0 / 40%))<br>dark: `color-black-a60` (rgb(0 0 0 / 60%)) |
| `--dui-color-shadow` | Shadow color | light: `color-black-a10` (rgb(0 0 0 / 10%))<br>dark: `color-black-a40` (rgb(0 0 0 / 40%)) |
| `--dui-font-body` | Body font stack | `--dui-font-stack-system-ui` (`system-ui, sans-serif`) |
| `--dui-font-mono` | Code font stack | `--dui-font-stack-monospace` (`ui-monospace`, …, `monospace`) |
| `--dui-font-weight-body` | Body weight | `font-weight-400` (400) |
| `--dui-font-weight-strong` | strong, labels, buttons, th | `font-weight-600` (600) |
| `--dui-font-weight-heading` | h1–h6 | `font-weight-700` (700) |
| `--dui-step--1` | small, captions | `--dui-font-size-fluid--1` |
| `--dui-step-0` | Body text, h6 | `--dui-font-size-fluid-0` |
| `--dui-step-1` | h5 | `--dui-font-size-fluid-1` |
| `--dui-step-2` | h4 | `--dui-font-size-fluid-2` |
| `--dui-step-3` | h3 | `--dui-font-size-fluid-3` |
| `--dui-step-4` | h2 | `--dui-font-size-fluid-4` |
| `--dui-step-5` | h1 | `--dui-font-size-fluid-5` |
| `--dui-font-size-code` | code, kbd, samp, pre (relative) | `font-size-relative-90` (0.9em) |
| `--dui-line-height-body` | Body text | `leading-160` (1.6) |
| `--dui-line-height-heading` | Headings, buttons, pre | `leading-125` (1.25) |
| `--dui-line-height-display` | h1 | `leading-110` (1.1) |
| `--dui-letter-spacing-heading` | h1, h2 | `tracking-tight` (-0.015em) |
| `--dui-measure` | Max line length for prose | `size-65ch` (65ch) |
| `--dui-space-3xs` | Space scale | `space-1` (0.125rem) |
| `--dui-space-2xs` | Space scale | `space-2` (0.25rem) |
| `--dui-space-xs` | Space scale | `space-3` (0.5rem) |
| `--dui-space-s` | Space scale | `space-4` (0.75rem) |
| `--dui-space-m` | Space scale; default flow rhythm and .stack gap | `space-5` (1rem) |
| `--dui-space-l` | Space scale; default .grid gap | `space-6` (1.5rem) |
| `--dui-space-xl` | Space scale; space above h1–h3 | `space-7` (2rem) |
| `--dui-space-2xl` | Space scale | `space-8` (3rem) |
| `--dui-space-3xl` | Space scale | `space-9` (4rem) |
| `--dui-size-target` | Min height of controls and buttons (WCAG 2.5.8 needs 24px; this gives 44px) | `size-2-75` (2.75rem) |
| `--dui-size-target-small` | Small buttons (32px: under 44px, over the 24px minimum) | `size-2` (2rem) |
| `--dui-size-target-large` | Large buttons | `size-3-25` (3.25rem) |
| `--dui-size-check` | Checkbox and radio size | `size-1-25` (1.25rem) |
| `--dui-size-column-min` | Default .grid min column width | `size-16` (16rem) |
| `--dui-size-menu-min` | Min width of menus and nav dropdowns | `size-12` (12rem) |
| `--dui-size-drawer` | Drawer width (all of the viewport when narrower) | `size-24` (24rem) |
| `--dui-radius-control` | Controls, buttons, inline code | `radius-2` (0.375rem) |
| `--dui-radius-surface` | Panels, pre, dialog, details, media | `radius-3` (0.625rem) |
| `--dui-radius-pill` | Fully rounded ends | `radius-round` (999rem) |
| `--dui-border-width` | Hairline width | `border-1` (1px) |
| `--dui-border-width-emphasis` | blockquote rule, alert start rule, invalid field | `border-4` (0.25rem) |
| `--dui-border-width-indicator` | Selected tab, current nav item (3:1 against the surface) | `border-3` (3px) |
| `--dui-underline-offset` | Link underline offset | `underline-offset-015em` (0.15em) |
| `--dui-underline-thickness` | Link underline | `underline-1` (0.0625em) |
| `--dui-underline-thickness-hover` | Link underline on hover | `underline-2` (0.125em) |
| `--dui-focus-width` | Focus outline width | `border-2` (2px) |
| `--dui-focus-offset` | Focus outline offset | `border-2` (2px) |
| `--dui-duration-fast` | Hover transitions (0s with reduced motion) | `duration-150` (150ms) |
| `--dui-duration-normal` | Larger transitions (0s with reduced motion) | `duration-250` (250ms) |
| `--dui-easing-standard` | Easing curve (linear with reduced motion) | `--dui-easing-ease-out` |
| `--dui-opacity-disabled` | Disabled controls, `disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"` | `opacity-60` (0.6) |
| `--dui-tint-amount` | How much of a tone goes into a tinted surface | `mix-8` (8%) |
| `--dui-border-tint-amount` | How much of the text color goes into a tinted border (badges) | `mix-35` (35%) |
| `--dui-color-link` | Links | `--dui-color-accent` |
| `--dui-color-focus` | Focus ring (3:1 against surfaces) | `--dui-color-accent` |
| `--dui-color-accent-hover` | Primary button hover | `color-mix()` of 82% `--dui-color-accent` with `--dui-color-text` |
| `--dui-font-heading` | Heading font stack | `--dui-font-body` |
| `--dui-shadow-raised` | dialog shadow | two-layer shadow using `--dui-color-shadow` |
| `--dui-color-accent-surface` | Accent badge background | `color-mix()` of `--dui-tint-amount` `--dui-color-accent` into `--dui-color-surface` |
| `--dui-color-success-surface` | Success badge background | same, with `--dui-color-success` |
| `--dui-color-warning-surface` | Warning badge background | same, with `--dui-color-warning` |
| `--dui-color-danger-surface` | Danger badge and alert background | same, with `--dui-color-danger` |
| `--dui-color-info-surface` | Info alert background | same, with `--dui-color-info` |
| `--dui-color-surface-inverse` | Tooltip background | `--dui-color-text` |
| `--dui-color-text-inverse` | Tooltip text | `--dui-color-surface` |

Derived (re-resolved on each theme scope): `--dui-color-link`, `--dui-color-focus`,
`--dui-color-accent-hover`, `--dui-font-heading`, `--dui-shadow-raised`,
`--dui-color-accent-surface`, `--dui-color-success-surface`, `--dui-color-warning-surface`,
`--dui-color-danger-surface`, `--dui-color-info-surface`, `--dui-color-surface-inverse`,
`--dui-color-text-inverse`.

## Opinions we hold

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/opinions-we-hold.html

Each of these is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** [logical properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_logical_properties_and_values)
  (`margin-block`, `inline-size`), so right-to-left and vertical writing modes work unchanged.
- **Our choice:** keep link underlines, because color alone is not enough to spot a link (WCAG 1.4.1).
- **Our choice:** system font stacks from [Modern Font Stacks](https://modernfontstacks.com/),
  because they cost no network requests and match the platform.
- **Our choice:** a fluid type scale with [`clamp()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/clamp)
  in `rem`, so text grows with the viewport and still respects the user's font size.
- **Our choice:** a 65ch measure for prose, near the commonly cited 45 to 75 characters per line
  ([WCAG 1.4.8 Visual Presentation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/visual-presentation.html) asks for 80 or fewer).
- **Our choice:** rhythm from the "lobotomized owl" selector (`* + *`) inside flow containers
  ([Heydon Pickering](https://alistapart.com/article/axiomatic-css-and-lobotomized-owls/)), wrapped in
  `:where()` so it has zero specificity.
- **Our choice:** `type="submit"` buttons get the accent fill and other buttons stay neutral,
  so the primary action is marked by its native type, with no class.
- **Our choice:** checkboxes, radios and range keep native rendering tinted with
  [`accent-color`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/accent-color), because
  native controls keep their platform accessibility.
- **Our choice:** each atom has one `data-<atom>` attribute whose value is a space-separated
  list (`data-button="primary small"`), matched with `~=`, instead of modifier classes. The
  other atom choices (button variants, focus rings, switch, field errors, badge tints) are
  listed with their reasons in the [atoms index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md#our-choices).
- **Our choice:** molecules follow the same rule (`data-card="link"`, `data-dialog="drawer end"`),
  or use the native element or ARIA role when that already says everything (`<search>`,
  `role="toolbar"`). The molecule choices are listed with their reasons in the
  [molecules index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/README.md#our-choices); the main ones:
  - **Our choice:** tabs select on focus (automatic activation), as the
    [APG recommends](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/#deciding-when-to-make-selection-automatically-follow-focus)
    when panels show at once; `activation="manual"` is available.
  - **Our choice:** the drawer is a `<dialog>` variant, so the browser handles modality, focus and
    <kbd>Esc</kbd> ([explainer](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/drawer.md)).
  - **Our choice:** a clickable card links its heading and stretches that link over the card, so the
    accessible name stays the heading ([explainer](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/card.md)).
  - **Our choice:** toasts never dismiss themselves and never take focus ([explainer](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/toast.md)).
- **Our choice:** layout primitives come from [Every Layout](https://every-layout.dev/)'s
  Stack, Cluster and Grid. Their custom properties are registered with
  [`@property`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@property) as non-inheriting,
  so a nested primitive keeps its own default.

## Layout primitives

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/layout-primitives.html

| Class | What it does | Custom properties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.stack` | Vertical flow with a gap | `--stack-gap` |
| `.cluster` | Wrapping inline group | `--cluster-gap`, `--cluster-justify`, `--cluster-align` |
| `.grid` | Auto-fit responsive grid, no media queries | `--grid-min`, `--grid-gap` |
| `[data-scroll="inline"]` | Scroll container for content wider than the screen, such as a data table | None |

```html
<div class="grid" style="--grid-min: 12rem">…</div>
```

On a `ul` or `ol`, the primitive also removes list markers and padding.

Wrap any table that may not fit a 320px screen in `data-scroll="inline"`, named by its caption:

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="orders-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="orders-caption">Recent orders</caption>
    …
  </table>
</section>
```

`tabindex="0"` makes it scrollable from the keyboard
([2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html), axe
[`scrollable-region-focusable`](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable)),
and a named `<section>` is a [region landmark](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section), so
screen reader users hear what that focus stop is. **Our choice:** `<section>` rather than
`<div role="region">`, because the native element already has the role. Data tables
may scroll sideways under [1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html);
the page itself must not. Never set `display: block` on the `<table>` instead: it can drop table
semantics in some browsers ([Adrian Roselli](https://adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html)).
A `<pre>` already scrolls (`overflow-x: auto`); authors MUST give every `<pre>` (and any
`data-scroll="inline"` container) `tabindex="0"` so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.

## Web components

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/web-components.html

HTML still has no element for tabs, menus, roving focus in a toolbar, hover tooltips or a toast
stack. For those, and only those, [`web-components/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/README.md) has one small
custom element each: `<dui-tabs>`, `<dui-menu>`, `<dui-toolbar>`, `<dui-tooltip>` and `<dui-toaster>`.

- **Light DOM.** No shadow root: the molecule CSS and your CSS style the markup directly.
- **Progressive enhancement.** The markup works before the script runs and with JavaScript off:
  tabs are a `<nav>` of in-page links and headed sections, toolbar buttons are Tab stops, a menu's
  popover still opens, a tooltip is still the button's description.
- **ARIA with behavior, or not at all.** An element adds roles such as `menu` or `tab` only together
  with the keyboard support those roles promise ([APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)).
- **Why each exists** is written at the top of its file, and the
  [web components index](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/web-components/README.md) lists them. Each one is a plain ES module with no
  dependencies and no build: `<script type="module" src="web-components/dui-tabs.js"></script>`.

## Explainers

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/explainers.html

A pattern with no native element and no APG pattern is written up like a platform proposal in
[`explainers/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/README.md): problem, use cases, goals and non-goals, markup and API,
keyboard, accessibility mappings, alternatives, prior art and open questions, with normative
text in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) keywords. The card, pagination, drawer
and toast molecules have one. Names follow HTML and ARIA conventions, so a pattern could map onto
a future native element or attribute.

## Tooling

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/tooling.html

`npm test` runs, in order, and fails if any step fails:

| Script | Tool | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lint:html` | [html-validate](https://html-validate.org/) | `examples/**/*.html` against `html-validate:recommended` |
| `lint:css` | [Stylelint](https://stylelint.io/) | `css/**/*.css` against `stylelint-config-standard` |
| `lint:tokens` | `scripts/check-tokens.mjs` | Semantic-only tokens and no literal colors or sizes outside `css/tokens/` |
| `test:a11y` | [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) + [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) | Every `examples/**/*.html` (atoms and molecules included) in light and dark, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`, including open dialogs and drawers, open popovers and menus, shown tooltips and toasts, every tab selected and every details expanded; no horizontal page overflow and no axe violations at 320×640 and 375×812; no external requests; token contrast pairs (atoms and molecules included) in the default and forest themes; rendered focus-ring and indicator contrast; atom and molecule states through accessibility APIs; molecule keyboard behavior against the APG; no-JavaScript fallbacks; fallbacks for engine-specific features; scoped theming of atoms and molecules |

Preview locally with `npm run serve` (a zero-dependency static server) and open
<http://127.0.0.1:4173/examples/base.html>. To run tests from two checkouts at once, give each its own port, e.g. `PORT=4273 npm test`.

Rule relaxations, each with its reason:

- **Stylelint `custom-property-pattern`** is replaced, not disabled. The standard kebab-case
  pattern rejects `--dui-step--1` (the double hyphen marks a negative step, a common naming for
  type scales below zero). The replacement still requires kebab-case and only allows names
  starting with `--dui-` or the documented layout properties (`--stack-*`, `--cluster-*`, `--grid-*`).
- **Engine-specific test**: the field test also reads the `invalid` state from the accessibility
  tree through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, which only Chromium offers; Firefox and WebKit run the
  rest of that test (attribute and accessible description). The molecule tests do the same for the
  expanded state of `<summary>` and of a `popovertarget` button, which browsers expose natively but
  Playwright's role engine does not compute; the other engines check the `open` attribute and the
  popover's visibility instead. No browser is skipped.
- **Feature fallbacks**: where every engine in the test run supports a feature (anchor positioning,
  `@starting-style`, `closedby`, `popover="hint"`), the molecule tests also exercise the fallback path
  by removing the feature in the page: deleting the `@supports` or `@starting-style` rules from the
  CSSOM, removing the `closedby` attribute, or setting `popover="manual"` (what `hint` falls back to).
- **Settling transitions**: axe and geometry checks wait for running CSS transitions to finish, so they
  measure final colors and positions rather than a frame mid-fade.
- **External-request check**: same-origin `blob:` URLs are allowed, because WebKit routes these
  in-memory objects through the request handler. Any other origin still fails the test.
- **html-validate**: none. `html-validate:recommended` is used as-is. Inline `style` attributes
  that set only custom properties are already allowed by its
  [`no-inline-style`](https://html-validate.org/rules/no-inline-style.html) default
  (`allowVariables: true`), which is how the layout primitives are configured.

## Tokens

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/index.html

All tokens are [CSS custom properties](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*) on `:root` with the `--dui-` prefix, in two tiers:

- **Primitive** tokens are named by what they are, such as `--dui-color-blue-600`. They are internal and may change in any release.
- **Semantic** tokens are named by what they are for, such as `--dui-color-accent`. They are the public theming API: renaming or removing one is a breaking change.

Base, layout, utility and component CSS use only semantic tokens; `npm run lint:tokens` enforces this. To theme, override semantic tokens: see [Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.md) and the [theming example](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/theming.html).

### Token files

One page per file in `css/tokens/`, grouped by its section comments, with a filter.

- [Primitive tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/primitives.md) (internal): 87 tokens in neutral gray, cool tint, hues, translucent black, for overlays and shadows, font stacks, font weights, fluid font sizes, line heights and tracking, spacing, sizes, radii, border widths, underline metrics, relative to the font, motion, opacity and mix amounts.
- [Semantic tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.md) (public theming API): 81 tokens in surfaces and text, borders, accent and status, type, space, sizes, shape, focus indicator, motion, state, dependent tokens, tinted surfaces for status badges, inverse pair for small overlays on top of content (tooltips): text and surface swapped.

### Tiers

From [Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/theming.md) in `PRINCIPLES.md`:

| Tier | File | Named by | Example | Public? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primitive | `css/tokens/primitives.css` | What it is | `--dui-color-blue-600: #3451d1;` `--dui-space-5: 1rem;` | No. Internal, may change in any release. |
| Semantic | `css/tokens/semantic.css` | What it is for | `--dui-color-accent: light-dark(var(--dui-color-blue-600), var(--dui-color-blue-400));` | **Yes.** The stable theming API. |

### How values are shown

**Written as** is the value in the file. **Light** and **dark** follow every `var()` through all token files and take one side of [`light-dark()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark); functions such as `color-mix()` and `clamp()` are left for the browser. Overrides under a condition, such as `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, are listed in the description. Previews are decorative; the text in each row is the reference.

## Primitive tokens

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/primitives.html

**Internal.** Raw values named by what they are, not by what they are for. Only css/tokens/semantic.css may reference these. Base, layout, utility and component CSS must use semantic tokens instead; `npm run lint:tokens` enforces this.

Primitives are NOT public API: they may be renamed, added or removed in any release. Theme with semantic tokens.

Custom properties: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/--*>

Defined in [`css/tokens/primitives.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/tokens/primitives.css): 87 tokens in 14 groups, one per section comment. See [Tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/index.md) for the two tiers.

**Written as** is the value in the file. **Light** and **dark** follow every `var()` through all token files and take one side of [`light-dark()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark); functions such as `color-mix()` and `clamp()` are left for the browser. Overrides under a condition, such as `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, are listed in the description. Previews are decorative; the text in each row is the reference.

### Fluid font sizes

A 1.2 ratio at small viewports growing to 1.25 at wide ones, interpolated with clamp(). <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/clamp>.

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-font-size-fluid--1` | `clamp(0.8333rem, 0.8101rem + 0.1159vw, 0.9rem)` | `clamp(0.8333rem, 0.8101rem + 0.1159vw, 0.9rem)` | No description yet. |

## Semantic tokens

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/semantic.html

**Public theming API.** Named by role. Each points at a primitive (css/tokens/primitives.css) or at another semantic token. Base, layout, utility and component CSS use only these. Renaming or removing one is a breaking change.

A theme is an override of these tokens on :root or on a scoped element. No rebuild. See PRINCIPLES.md, "Theming".

Colors use light-dark(), which picks a value from the used color-scheme of the element where the token is read. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark>

Defined in [`css/tokens/semantic.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/tokens/semantic.css): 81 tokens in 13 groups, one per section comment. See [Tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/index.md) for the two tiers.

**Written as** is the value in the file. **Light** and **dark** follow every `var()` through all token files and take one side of [`light-dark()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark); functions such as `color-mix()` and `clamp()` are left for the browser. Overrides under a condition, such as `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, are listed in the description. Previews are decorative; the text in each row is the reference.

| Token | Light | Dark | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dui-color-surface` | `#fff` | `#12151b` | Page and control background (from PRINCIPLES.md) |

| `--dui-color-surface-sunken` | `#eceef2` | `#252a34` | Recessed areas: code, button hover (from PRINCIPLES.md) |

## Base elements

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.html

Native HTML elements styled by the base layer, with no classes.

### API

No classes: write semantic HTML and the base layer styles it.

- `data-color-scheme="light" | "dark"`

### Files in css/base/

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [`css/base/document.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/document.css) | Document, color scheme, rhythm and focus. |
| [`css/base/forms.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/forms.css) |  |
| [`css/base/interactive.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/interactive.css) |  |
| [`css/base/media.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/media.css) |  |
| [`css/base/tables.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/tables.css) |  |
| [`css/base/typography.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/base/typography.css) |  |

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/base.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/base.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/base.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Preformatted code

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/domestic.css">

:root {
  --dui-color-accent: light-dark(#7a2e8c, #e2a8f0);
}
```

### Accessibility

Each point below is stated in a `css/base/` comment or in [PRINCIPLES.md](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/index.md).

- Links keep their underline, so color is never the only cue ([WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)).
- Every focusable element shows a `:focus-visible` outline in `--dui-color-focus`; under `forced-colors: active` it switches to the system `highlight` color ([WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html)).
- `scroll-padding-block` keeps focused and targeted elements clear of sticky edges ([WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html)).
- Text controls, buttons and summaries are at least `--dui-size-target` tall ([WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)).
- Checkboxes, radios and range keep native rendering, tinted with `accent-color`.
- Open a `<dialog>` with `showModal()` or a `command="show-modal"` button so the browser handles focus, <kbd>Esc</kbd> and inertness ([APG modal dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)).
- Duration tokens become `0s` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- The CSS cannot add semantics for you: give every control a `<label>`, group controls with `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, give tables a `<caption>` and `th` with `scope`, and give meaningful images `alt` text (see [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md)).

### Specs

- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color-scheme](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color-scheme)
- **Other**: [alistapart.com/article/axiomatic-css-and-lobotomized-owls/](https://alistapart.com/article/axiomatic-css-and-lobotomized-owls/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:focus-visible](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:focus-visible)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html)
- **W3C**: [www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/accent-color](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/accent-color)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/dialog](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/dialog)
- **APG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

## Visually hidden

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/utilities/visually-hidden.html

Hides content visually but keeps it in the accessibility tree.

```text
class="visually-hidden"
```

Layout primitives and utilities are classes, not `data-*` attributes; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

## Layouts

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/index.html

Layout primitives arrange their children and nothing else; see [Layout primitives](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/layout-primitives.md). Each has one class and is tuned with custom properties. Page layouts such as the app shell are listed with their status.

### All layouts

- [Cluster](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/cluster.md): An inline group that wraps onto new lines (buttons, tags, nav links).
- [Grid](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/grid.md): A responsive grid: as many columns as fit, each at least --grid-min wide, never wider than the container.
- [Scroll](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/scroll.md): A scroll container for content wider than the screen (data tables, long code, wide media), so it scrolls on its own instead of widening the page (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow allows two-dimensional scrolling for data tables: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html>).
- [Stack](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/stack.md): Vertical flow with a consistent gap between children.
- [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md): The frame of an application: header, primary sidebar, main content and an optional auxiliary sidebar. Coming in M3b.
- [Dashboard](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dashboard.md): A grid of summary sections, each with a heading, that reflows to fit the screen. Coming in M3b.
- [List-detail](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.md): A list of items beside the details of the selected one, stacked on narrow screens. Coming in M3b.
- [Split](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.md): Two regions side by side at a set ratio, stacked on narrow screens. Coming in M3b.

## Cluster

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/cluster.html

An inline group that wraps onto new lines (buttons, tags, nav links).

### API

```text
class="cluster"
--cluster-gap       space between items   (default: var(--dui-space-s))
--cluster-justify   justify-content value (default: flex-start)
--cluster-align     align-items value     (default: center)
```

Layout primitives and utilities are classes, not `data-*` attributes; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

### Live example

```html
<ul class="cluster" style="--cluster-justify: space-between">…</ul>
```

### Notes

Pattern: "The Cluster", Every Layout (<https://every-layout.dev/layouts/cluster/>), built with flex-wrap and gap.

The custom properties do not inherit, so nested clusters keep their defaults.

## Grid

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/grid.html

A responsive grid: as many columns as fit, each at least --grid-min wide, never wider than the container.

### API

```text
class="grid"
--grid-min   minimum column width (default: var(--dui-size-column-min))
--grid-gap   gap between cells    (default: var(--dui-space-l))
```

Layout primitives and utilities are classes, not `data-*` attributes; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

### Live example

There is no standalone example page for grid yet. These example pages use it: [Base elements](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/base.html), [Theming](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/theming.html), [Form controls](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/controls.html), [Atoms showcase](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/index.html), [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/card.html), [Molecules showcase](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/index.html).

### Markup

From the `Example` block in [`css/layout/grid.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/layout/grid.css):

```html
<div class="grid" style="--grid-min: 12rem">…</div>
```

### Notes

No media queries. Pattern: "RAM" (repeat, auto-fit, minmax), see <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat#auto-fit> and "The Grid", Every Layout (<https://every-layout.dev/layouts/grid/>).

The custom properties do not inherit, so nested grids keep their defaults.

### Accessibility

The CSS header comment has no accessibility notes. See the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat#auto-fit](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/repeat#auto-fit)
- **Other**: [every-layout.dev/layouts/grid/](https://every-layout.dev/layouts/grid/)

## Scroll

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/scroll.html

A scroll container for content wider than the screen (data tables, long code, wide media), so it scrolls on its own instead of widening the page (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow allows two-dimensional scrolling for data tables: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html>).

### API

```text
data-scroll="inline"   scroll along the inline axis (left/right in English)
```

Layout primitives and utilities are classes, not `data-*` attributes; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

### Live example

There is no standalone example page for scroll yet. These example pages use it: [Base elements](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/base.html), [Badge](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/badge.html), [Atoms showcase](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/index.html), [Quiet link](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/link.html).

### Markup

From the `Example` block in [`css/layout/scroll.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/layout/scroll.css):

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="orders-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="orders-caption">Recent orders</caption>
    …
  </table>
</section>
```

### Notes

Built on overflow-x: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow-x>

tabindex="0" lets keyboard users scroll it with the arrow keys (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, axe rule scrollable-region-focusable: <https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable>). A \<section> named with aria-labelledby is a region landmark (<https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section>), so screen readers announce what the focus stop is. Our choice: \<section> over \<div role="region">, because the native element already has the role. Any element works if it has role="region" and a name. The table itself keeps display: table. Changing a table's display can drop its table semantics in some browsers (Adrian Roselli, "Tables, CSS Display Properties, and ARIA": <https://adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html>).

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: A scroll container for content wider than the screen (data tables, long code, wide media), so it scrolls on its own instead of widening the page (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow allows two-dimensional scrolling for data tables: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html>). tabindex="0" lets keyboard users scroll it with the arrow keys (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, axe rule scrollable-region-focusable: <https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable>). A \<section> named with aria-labelledby is a region landmark (<https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section>), so screen readers announce what the focus stop is. Changing a table's display can drop its table semantics in some browsers (Adrian Roselli, "Tables, CSS Display Properties, and ARIA": <https://adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html>).

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow-x](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/overflow-x)
- **Other**: [dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.10/scrollable-region-focusable)
- **W3C**: [www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-section)
- **Other**: [adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html](https://adrianroselli.com/2018/02/tables-css-display-properties-and-aria.html)

### Source

- [`css/layout/scroll.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/layout/scroll.css)

## Atoms

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/atoms/index.html

Atoms add the minimum on top of the [base layer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md): plain HTML already looks right, and an atom covers what a native element cannot say on its own. Components use one `data-<component>` attribute each; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api). The levels follow [atomic design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/chapter-2/); planned [patterns](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md) are listed at their level with their status.

### Atoms

- [Text helpers](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/text.md): Lead, small and muted text helpers from domestic-ui, with copyable markup. API: `data-text="lead | small | muted"` (combinable).
- [Quiet link](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/link.md): A link that takes the surrounding text color and keeps its underline, for dense UI. API: `data-link="quiet"` on `<a href>`.
- [Buttons](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/button.md): Button variants, sizes, link buttons and honest disabled and loading states. API: `data-button="[primary | secondary | quiet] [small | large]"` on `<button>`, `<input type=submit|button|reset>`, `<a href>`; states `disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, `aria-busy="true"`.
- [Form controls](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/controls.md): Native form controls as styled by the domestic-ui base layer, with copyable markup. API: No API; native elements.
- [Switch](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/switch.md): An on/off switch built on a native checkbox with role switch, following the APG Switch pattern. API: `role="switch"` on `<input type="checkbox">`.
- [Field](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/field.md): Label, control, hint and error message wired with aria-describedby and aria-invalid. API: `data-field` on the wrapper, `data-field="hint"` and `data-field="error"` on the messages.
- [Badge](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/badge.md): Inline status labels with tone variants that meet WCAG AA contrast. API: `data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"`.

### Our choices

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** one `data-<atom>` attribute per atom, whose value is a space-separated list matched with [`~=`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Attribute_selectors). One attribute is one API to learn, it reads as a sentence (`data-button="primary small"`), and it cannot pile up like modifier classes.
- **Our choice:** `data-button` with no variant word keeps the native default (a submit button is primary, everything else is secondary), so M1 markup keeps working and the attribute is only needed when the native type does not match the emphasis you want.
- **Our choice:** the quiet button uses the accent color for its text, so it still reads as interactive without a border. Use it next to other buttons, not inside running text, where a real link belongs.
- **Our choice:** primary buttons add an inner focus ring in their text color on top of the shared outline, so the indicator contrasts with the fill as well as the surface. This is the double-ring technique described in [WCAG technique C40](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C40).
- **Our choice:** small buttons are 32px tall: below the 44px default, above the [24px minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html).
- **Our choice:** `aria-disabled="true"` looks exactly like `disabled`. Prefer native `disabled`; use `aria-disabled` when users should be able to reach the control and read why it is unavailable.
- **Our choice:** the field's error text starts with the word "Error:" in the markup, rather than a CSS icon, so every user and every screen reader gets it with no extra API. Invalid controls also get a thick start border, a shape change as well as a color change.
- **Our choice:** errors are tied to controls with `aria-describedby`, not `aria-errormessage`, because `aria-describedby` has broader screen reader support today (see the support notes on [MDN `aria-errormessage`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-errormessage)).
- **Our choice:** the switch is the native checkbox with `role="switch"`, drawn with `appearance: none` and one pseudo-element. The thumb moves and changes color, and forced-colors mode gets explicit system colors.
- **Our choice:** badge tones are 8% of the tone mixed into the surface, with the tone as text. The tinted surfaces are derived tokens (`--dui-color-*-surface`), so a theme that changes the surface or a tone re-tints badges with no extra overrides.
- **Our choice:** a field is an atom here, not a molecule, because a control is not usable without its label, hint and error. Larger compositions (forms, cards, headers) are molecules and organisms for later milestones.

### Not shipped, and why

| Candidate | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Divider | Cut. `<hr>` is the native thematic break and is already styled in the base layer. A class would duplicate it. |
| Avatar | Cut. There is no standard or APG pattern for it; it is an `<img alt>` with a radius and a size, which the base layer and one line of your CSS already give. Revisit with a real use case (initials fallback, image loading). |
| Icon sizing | Cut. domestic-ui ships no icon set, so there is nothing to size consistently yet. Inside buttons, icons already line up through the button's `inline-flex` and `gap`. |
| Danger button variant | Not added. Not requested, and a destructive action is better marked by its label and a confirmation `<dialog>` than by color. Easy to add later as one more variant word. |
| Spinner for loading | Not added. The honest state is the changed label plus `aria-busy`; a spinner that replaces the label hides it from everyone. |

## Text helpers

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/text.html

Lead, small and muted text helpers from domestic-ui, with copyable markup.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`data-text="lead | small | muted"` (combinable)

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/text.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/text.css):

```text
data-text="lead | small | muted"
Values are a space-separated list, so they combine: data-text="small muted".
```

`data-text` follows the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api): one attribute, its value space-separated words matched with `~=`; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/text.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/text.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/text.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Lead paragraph

```html
<p data-text="lead">Plan your week in five minutes. Everything else stays out of the way.</p>
<p>Regular body text follows at the normal size.</p>
```

#### Small and muted

```html
<p data-text="small">Prices include tax.</p>
<p data-text="muted">Shared with 3 people.</p>
<p data-text="small muted">Last updated <time datetime="2026-05-03">3 May 2026</time>.</p>
```

### Notes

Presentation helpers for prose. They change size or color only, never meaning: use \<small> for side comments and \<strong>/\<em> for importance or stress, as the HTML standard defines them. <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-small-element> code, kbd and samp are already styled in css/base/typography.css.

Muted text uses --dui-color-text-muted, which is tested at 4.5:1 on every surface (WCAG 1.4.3: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html>).

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: Muted text uses --dui-color-text-muted, which is tested at 4.5:1 on every surface (WCAG 1.4.3: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html>).

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **WHATWG text-level semantics**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html)
- **WCAG 1.4.3**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-small-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-small-element)

- [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md)

## Quiet link

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/link.html

A link that takes the surrounding text color and keeps its underline, for dense UI.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`data-link="quiet"` on `<a href>`

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/link.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/link.css):

```text
data-link="quiet"   on <a href>
```

`data-link` follows the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api): one attribute, its value space-separated words matched with `~=`; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/link.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/link.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/link.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### In a table

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="orders-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="orders-caption">Recent orders</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th scope="col">Order</th><th scope="col">Customer</th><th scope="col">Total</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td><a href="#table-title" data-link="quiet">#1042</a></td><td>Ada Lovelace</td><td>€120.00</td></tr>
      <tr><td><a href="#table-title" data-link="quiet">#1041</a></td><td>Alan Turing</td><td>€48.50</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</section>
```

#### In muted metadata

```html
<p data-text="small muted">Posted by <a href="#meta-title" data-link="quiet">Grace Hopper</a> in <a href="#meta-title" data-link="quiet">Compilers</a>.</p>
```

### Notes

A link that takes the color of the text around it, for dense UI such as table cells, footers and metadata lines where many accent-colored links would be noisy. It keeps its underline, so color is never the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html> <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element>

Visited links keep the surrounding color too. The surrounding text color already meets 4.5:1, so the link does as well.

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: It keeps its underline, so color is never the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html> <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element>

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **WHATWG `a`**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element)
- **WCAG 1.4.1**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/atoms/link.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/link.css)
- [`examples/atoms/link.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/link.html)
- [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md)

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent

## Buttons

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/button.html

Button variants, sizes, link buttons and honest disabled and loading states.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`data-button="[primary | secondary | quiet] [small | large]"` on `<button>`, `<input type=submit|button|reset>`, `<a href>`; states `disabled`, `aria-disabled="true"`, `aria-busy="true"`

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/button.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/button.css):

```text
data-button="[primary | secondary | quiet] [small | large]"
A space-separated list: at most one variant word and one size word.
Works on <button>, <input type="submit|button|reset"> and <a href>.
No variant word keeps the native default: type="submit" is primary,
other buttons and links are secondary.
```

`data-button` follows the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api): one attribute, its value space-separated words matched with `~=`; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA.

### States

From the `States` block in [`css/components/atoms/button.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/button.css):

```text
disabled              Native. Removed from the tab order, not submitted.
aria-disabled="true"  Looks disabled and is exposed as disabled, but stays
                      focusable so a description can explain why. Your script
                      must ignore activation. https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols
                      https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-disabled
aria-busy="true"      Work in progress. Change the visible label too
                      ("Saving…") and announce the result in a role="status"
                      region; nothing here hides the label.
                      https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-busy
```

### Sizes

From the `Sizes` block in [`css/components/atoms/button.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/button.css):

```text
default and large are at least 44px tall. small is 32px: below the
44px default but above the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum).
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html
```

### Focus

From the `Focus` block in [`css/components/atoms/button.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/button.css):

```text
every variant keeps the base :focus-visible outline. Filled (primary)
buttons add an inner ring in their text color, so the indicator contrasts
with the fill as well as with the surface (WCAG 1.4.11, 2.4.13).
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html
```

### Our choice

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** `data-button` with no variant word keeps the native default (a submit button is primary, everything else is secondary), so M1 markup keeps working and the attribute is only needed when the native type does not match the emphasis you want.
- **Our choice:** the quiet button uses the accent color for its text, so it still reads as interactive without a border. Use it next to other buttons, not inside running text, where a real link belongs.
- **Our choice:** primary buttons add an inner focus ring in their text color on top of the shared outline, so the indicator contrasts with the fill as well as the surface. This is the double-ring technique described in [WCAG technique C40](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C40).
- **Our choice:** small buttons are 32px tall: below the 44px default, above the [24px minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html).
- **Our choice:** `aria-disabled="true"` looks exactly like `disabled`. Prefer native `disabled`; use `aria-disabled` when users should be able to reach the control and read why it is unavailable.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/button.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/button.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/button.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Variants

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary">Primary</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="secondary">Secondary</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="quiet">Quiet</button>
</div>
```

#### Native default

```html
<form action="#native-title" class="cluster">
  <button type="submit">Publish</button>
  <button type="submit" name="draft" value="1" data-button="secondary">Save draft</button>
  <button type="reset" data-button="quiet">Clear</button>
</form>
```

#### Sizes

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary small">Small</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="primary">Default</button>
  <button type="button" data-button="primary large">Large</button>
</div>
```

#### Links that look like buttons

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <a href="#links-title" data-button="primary">Create account</a>
  <a href="#links-title" data-button="secondary">Read the guide</a>
  <a href="#links-title" data-button="quiet">Skip for now</a>
</div>
```

#### Disabled

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary" disabled>Delete</button>
  <button type="button" disabled>Archive</button>
</div>
```

#### Disabled but focusable

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-button="primary" aria-disabled="true" aria-describedby="publish-why">Publish</button>
  <p id="publish-why" data-text="small muted">Add a title before publishing.</p>
</div>
```

#### Loading

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" id="save-demo" data-button="primary">Save changes</button>
  <p id="save-status" role="status" data-text="small muted"></p>
</div>
```

### Notes

Plain \<button> is already styled in css/base/forms.css: type="submit" gets the accent fill, every other button is neutral. This atom adds explicit variants, a size scale, aria-disabled and aria-busy states, and lets a link (\<a href>) look like a button while keeping link semantics. <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element> APG button pattern: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/>

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: This atom adds explicit variants, a size scale, aria-disabled and aria-busy states, and lets a link (\<a href>) look like a button while keeping link semantics. <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element> APG button pattern: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/>

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

The header comment's `States`, `Sizes`, `Focus` blocks are shown above under their own headings.

### Specs

- **WHATWG `button`**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element)
- **APG Button**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/)
- **APG focusability of disabled controls**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#focusabilityofdisabledcontrols)
- **MDN `aria-disabled`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-disabled](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-disabled)
- **MDN `aria-busy`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-busy](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-busy)
- **WCAG 2.5.8**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html)

No API; native elements

```html
  </div>

  </div>
  <div>
```
