## Switch

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/switch.html

An on/off switch built on a native checkbox with role switch, following the APG Switch pattern.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`role="switch"` on `<input type="checkbox">`

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/switch.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/switch.css):

```text
role="switch"   on <input type="checkbox">; no class needed.
```

No `data-*` attribute: the API is native HTML and ARIA. See the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api).

### Our choice

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** the switch is the native checkbox with `role="switch"`, drawn with `appearance: none` and one pseudo-element. The thumb moves and changes color, and forced-colors mode gets explicit system colors.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/switch.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/switch.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/switch.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Off, on and disabled

```html
<div class="stack" style="--stack-gap: 0">
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="alerts"> Email alerts</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="digest" checked> Weekly digest</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="beta" disabled> Beta features</label>
</div>
```

#### In a fieldset

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Privacy</legend>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="profile-public" checked> Public profile</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="show-email"> Show email address</label>
</fieldset>
```

### Notes

An on/off control built on a native checkbox with role="switch", as in the APG Switch pattern ("Switch Example Using HTML Checkbox Input"). The checkbox brings focus, Space to toggle, form submission and the :checked state; role="switch" tells assistive technology to announce "on/off" instead of "checked/not checked". APG: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/> ARIA in HTML allows role="switch" on input type=checkbox: <https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-input-checkbox> MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/switch_role>

Keep the label the same in both states (APG): the state is "on" or "off", not a different label. Wrapping the input in its \<label> also makes the whole label the click target (44px tall, see css/base/forms.css).

State does not rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the thumb moves to the end and changes from outline color to the contrast color, and the track fills. Track border and thumb are 3:1 against the surface (WCAG 1.4.11). Forced colors: system colors are set explicitly so both states stay visible. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors>

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: An on/off control built on a native checkbox with role="switch", as in the APG Switch pattern ("Switch Example Using HTML Checkbox Input"). The checkbox brings focus, Space to toggle, form submission and the :checked state; role="switch" tells assistive technology to announce "on/off" instead of "checked/not checked". APG: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/> ARIA in HTML allows role="switch" on input type=checkbox: <https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-input-checkbox> MDN: <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/switch_role> Keep the label the same in both states (APG): the state is "on" or "off", not a different label. State does not rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the thumb moves to the end and changes from outline color to the contrast color, and the track fills. Track border and thumb are 3:1 against the surface (WCAG 1.4.11). Forced colors: system colors are set explicitly so both states stay visible. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors>

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **APG Switch**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/switch/)
- **ARIA in HTML**: [www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-input-checkbox](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-input-checkbox)
- **MDN `switch` role**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/switch_role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/switch_role)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/forced-colors)

## Field

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/field.html

Label, control, hint and error message wired with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`data-field` on the wrapper, `data-field="hint"` and `data-field="error"` on the messages

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/field.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/field.css):

```text
data-field              on the wrapper (a <div>, or a <fieldset> for groups)
data-field="hint"       on the hint
data-field="error"      on the error message
```

`data-field` follows the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api): one attribute, its value space-separated words matched with `~=`; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA.

### Our choice

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** the field's error text starts with the word "Error:" in the markup, rather than a CSS icon, so every user and every screen reader gets it with no extra API. Invalid controls also get a thick start border, a shape change as well as a color change.
- **Our choice:** a field is an atom here, not a molecule, because a control is not usable without its label, hint and error. Larger compositions (forms, cards, headers) are molecules and organisms for later milestones.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/field.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/field.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/field.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### With a hint

```html
<div data-field>
  <label for="f-name">Display name</label>
  <input id="f-name" name="display-name" type="text" autocomplete="nickname" aria-describedby="f-name-hint">
  <p id="f-name-hint" data-field="hint">Shown next to your comments.</p>
</div>
```

#### With a hint and an error

```html
<div data-field>
  <label for="f-email">Email</label>
  <input id="f-email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" value="ada@" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="f-email-hint f-email-error">
  <p id="f-email-hint" data-field="hint">We only use this to reply.</p>
  <p id="f-email-error" data-field="error">Error: enter an email address like name@example.com.</p>
</div>
```

#### Native validation

```html
<form action="#native-title" class="stack">
  <div data-field>
    <label for="f-code">Invite code</label>
    <input id="f-code" name="code" type="text" required minlength="6" aria-describedby="f-code-hint">
    <p id="f-code-hint" data-field="hint">Six characters or more.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="cluster">
    <button type="submit">Join</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

#### A group with an error

```html
<fieldset data-field aria-describedby="f-size-error">
  <legend>Size</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m"> Medium</label>
  <p id="f-size-error" data-field="error">Error: choose a size.</p>
</fieldset>
```

### Notes

Groups one control with its label, an optional hint and an optional error message, and styles the invalid state. The wiring is plain HTML and ARIA; this file only lays it out.

- The \<label for> names the control (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html> <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html> - Hint and error ids go in the control's aria-describedby, so they become its accessible description. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby> - When the value is wrong, set aria-invalid="true" on the control and show the error as text (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid> - Native constraint validation also gets the invalid look, via :user-invalid (only after the user has interacted). <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid>

Not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the error text starts with "Error:" (write it in the markup so every user and screen reader gets it), and an invalid control gets a thick start border as well as the danger color. Hide an error that does not apply with the hidden attribute and remove its id from aria-describedby.

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: The wiring is plain HTML and ARIA; this file only lays it out. - The \<label for> names the control (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html> <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html> - Hint and error ids go in the control's aria-describedby, so they become its accessible description. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby> - When the value is wrong, set aria-invalid="true" on the control and show the error as text (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification). <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid> - Native constraint validation also gets the invalid look, via :user-invalid (only after the user has interacted). <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid> Not color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the error text starts with "Error:" (write it in the markup so every user and screen reader gets it), and an invalid control gets a thick start border as well as the danger color. Hide an error that does not apply with the hidden attribute and remove its id from aria-describedby.

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **WCAG 3.3.1**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification.html)
- **WCAG 3.3.2**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)
- **WCAG 1.3.1**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html)
- **MDN `aria-describedby`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-describedby)
- **MDN `aria-invalid`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-invalid)
- **MDN `:user-invalid`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/:user-invalid)

## Badge

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/atoms/badge.html

Inline status labels with tone variants that meet WCAG AA contrast.

### API

From the index in [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md):

`data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"`

The `API` block in [`css/components/atoms/badge.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/badge.css):

```text
data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"
(empty means neutral)
```

`data-badge` follows the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api): one attribute, its value space-separated words matched with `~=`; state is carried by native attributes and ARIA.

### Our choice

From [`css/components/atoms/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** badge tones are 8% of the tone mixed into the surface, with the tone as text. The tinted surfaces are derived tokens (`--dui-color-*-surface`), so a theme that changes the surface or a tone re-tints badges with no extra overrides.

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/badge.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/atoms/badge.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/atoms/badge.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Tones

```html
<p class="cluster">
  <span data-badge>Draft</span>
  <span data-badge="accent">New</span>
  <span data-badge="success">Paid</span>
  <span data-badge="warning">Due soon</span>
  <span data-badge="danger">Overdue</span>
</p>
```

#### In context

```html
<section data-scroll="inline" aria-labelledby="invoices-caption" tabindex="0">
  <table>
    <caption id="invoices-caption">Invoices</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr><th scope="col">Invoice</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>INV-031</td><td><span data-badge="success">Paid</span></td></tr>
      <tr><td>INV-032</td><td><span data-badge="danger">Overdue</span></td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</section>
```

### Notes

A short inline status label ("Draft", "Paid", "Overdue"). Static text, not interactive: there is no native badge element and no ARIA role is needed, the text itself is the content. If a badge must be clickable, put a real \<button> or \<a href> around it, not a click handler on it. Native first: <https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1>

The tone is a hint, not the message: the words carry the meaning (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). If a badge sits next to something it labels only by position, say so in text, for example "Status: Paid" with .visually-hidden on "Status:". Text on each tone meets 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3); npm test checks every tone. <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html>

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: Static text, not interactive: there is no native badge element and no ARIA role is needed, the text itself is the content. Native first: <https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1> The tone is a hint, not the message: the words carry the meaning (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). Text on each tone meets 4.5:1 (WCAG 1.4.3); npm test checks every tone. <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html>

See also the spec links below and the [Accessibility baseline](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/principles/accessibility-baseline-wcag-22-aa.md) principle.

### Specs

- **WCAG 1.4.3**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html)
- **WCAG 1.4.1**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)
- **Using ARIA rule 1**: [www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1](https://www.w3.org/TR/using-aria/#rule1)

## Molecules

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/molecules/index.html

Components use one `data-<component>` attribute each; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api). The levels follow [atomic design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/chapter-2/); planned [patterns](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md) are listed at their level with their status.

### Molecules

- [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md): Messages about status, from notices in the page to live alerts for important, time-sensitive changes. Available.
- [Breadcrumb](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.md): The path to the current page as an ordered list of links in a labelled `<nav>`. Available.
- [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md): A self-contained item, such as a product or an article teaser, on a raised surface. Available.
- [Disclosure](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/disclosure.md): A summary that shows or hides more content, built on `<details>` and `<summary>`. Available.
- [Menu button](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md): A button that opens a menu of actions. Available.
- [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md): Links to the pages of a long list of results. Available.
- [Popover](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.md): Content shown on top of the page from a button, with the `popover` attribute. Available.
- [Search](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.md): A search form in a `<search>` landmark with an `<input type="search">`. Available.
- [Tabs](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md): Sections of content shown one at a time, chosen from a list of tabs. Available.
- [Toolbar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.md): A row of related controls that is one stop in the tab order. Available.
- [Typeahead](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md): A text field that suggests values as you type, with `<datalist>` first and an APG combobox only where `<datalist>` falls short. Coming in M3.

### Our choices

From [`css/components/molecules/README.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/README.md). Each is a choice between valid options, not a standard.

- **Our choice:** native first, even where it differs from the APG example. The accordion is `<details name>`, so there are no heading wrappers and no arrow keys between headers (both optional in the APG); nav groups are `<details>` rather than scripted disclosure buttons, so they do not close on <kbd>Esc</kbd>. Both work with no script and keep find-in-page.
- **Our choice:** the drawer is a `<dialog>` variant (`data-dialog="drawer"`), not a new element or a popover, so it gets modality, inertness, focus handling and <kbd>Esc</kbd> from the browser. See [drawer.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/drawer.md).
- **Our choice:** dialog and drawer motion uses `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, declared after a plain transition, so engines without them simply open and close instantly. Duration tokens are `0s` under reduced motion.
- **Our choice:** anchored popovers fall back to the bottom center of the viewport where CSS anchor positioning is missing, rather than the browser's default center, so they never cover the middle of the content.
- **Our choice:** automatic tab activation (selection follows focus), as the [APG recommends](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/#deciding-when-to-make-selection-automatically-follow-focus) when panels show without delay; `activation="manual"` is one attribute away.
- **Our choice:** tabs are written as a `<nav>` of in-page links and `<section>` panels, so they read as a table of contents with JavaScript off. Once upgraded, each panel's first heading is visually hidden (it repeats the tab label) but stays in the accessibility tree.
- **Our choice:** `<dui-menu>` adds `role="menu"` and `role="menuitem"` itself. Without the script there are no menu roles, so assistive technology is never promised arrow keys that do not work. A list of links is never a menu; use a disclosure.
- **Our choice:** `<dui-toolbar>` keeps `role="toolbar"` in the markup, because a labelled group of Tab stops is still correct without the script; only the roving focus is added.
- **Our choice:** navigation lists (nav, tabs, pagination) drop the link underline, because their role is clear from the list ([F73](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F73) is about links in running text); hover brings it back. Breadcrumb links keep it, because they read as text.
- **Our choice:** "current" is never color alone: the nav item gets an accent bar, a tint and bold text; the current page in pagination is filled and bold; the selected tab gets a bar and full-strength text.
- **Our choice:** the current page in pagination stays a link with `aria-current="page"`, and a disabled Previous or Next is an `<a>` with no `href`, which HTML defines as a placeholder: not focusable and not a link. See [pagination.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/pagination.md).
- **Our choice:** a clickable card puts the link on its heading and stretches the link's hit area with a pseudo-element, so the card's accessible name is the heading and secondary actions in the footer stay separate links. See [card.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/card.md).
- **Our choice:** alert tones start with a word in the markup ("Warning:"), like the field's "Error:", and add a decorative icon drawn in CSS with empty alternative text.
- **Our choice:** an `info` tone with its own token (`--dui-color-info`) instead of reusing the accent, so a green or red brand accent never makes an informational message look like success or danger.
- **Our choice:** toasts never dismiss themselves and never take focus; each has a Dismiss button, and the region is a fixed element in the page (not a popover) so server-rendered messages show with JavaScript off. See [toast.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/toast.md).
- **Our choice:** the tooltip uses inverse colors (`--dui-color-surface-inverse` and `--dui-color-text-inverse`, derived from the text and surface tokens), so every theme gets a readable tooltip with no extra overrides.

### Not shipped, and why

| Candidate | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Combobox, typeahead, datalist | Later milestone (`dui-combobox`). It needs the APG Combobox pattern and a listbox, which is a bigger piece of work. |
| Vertical tabs | Not added. The APG allows them (`aria-orientation="vertical"`), but they need a different layout and Up/Down keys; add them with a real use case. |
| Menubar, submenus | Not added. Application menubars are rare on the web, and submenus are hard to use; a menu button covers actions. |
| Arrow-key navigation between accordion headers | Not added. It is optional in the APG Accordion pattern, and native `<details>` gives every summary a Tab stop. |
| Auto-dismissing toasts | Not added on purpose; see Our choices and [toast.md](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/explainers/toast.md). |
| `interestfor` tooltips | Not used yet. It is the coming standard for hover and focus invokers but ships only in Chromium; `<dui-tooltip>` does the job until it is interoperable. |

## Organisms

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/organisms/index.html

Components use one `data-<component>` attribute each; see the [component API convention](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/index.md#component-api). The levels follow [atomic design](https://atomicdesign.bradfrost.com/chapter-2/); planned [patterns](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md) are listed at their level with their status.

### Organisms

- [Dialog and drawer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md): A modal `<dialog>`, either centered or as a drawer along one edge of the viewport. Available.
- [Site navigation](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/nav.md): The main links of a site in a `<nav>` landmark, with the current page marked. Available.
- [Data table](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.md): Rows of records in a native `<table>` with a caption, header cells and optional sorting. Coming in M3b.
- [Filter bar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/filter-bar.md): A row of native form controls that narrows a list or table. Coming in M3b.
- [Large forms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/large-forms.md): Long forms split into labelled groups, in one or more columns. Coming in M3b.

## Patterns

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.html

Where a standard exists, a native HTML element or a [WAI-ARIA APG pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/), the pattern follows it and links to it. Where none exists, the pattern is written as close to plain HTML as possible and labeled **Our choice:** with one line on why.

A pattern page fills in on its own when its example page or CSS file lands. Until then it says which milestone it is planned for. To go from a plain page to a full app step by step, read [From a simple site to an ERP app](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/simple-site-to-erp-app.md).

### M3: Molecules and navigation patterns

| Pattern | Level | Status | Follows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md) | molecule | Available | [APG Alert pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/) |
| [Breadcrumb](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.md) | molecule | Available | [APG Breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/) |
| [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md) | molecule | Available | **Our choice:** No native element or APG pattern exists; an `<article>` with a heading, where the heading holds the one link, so the whole card is not one long link name. |
| [Dialog and drawer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md) | organism | Available | [HTML `<dialog>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element), [APG Dialog (Modal) pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/) |
| [Disclosure](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/disclosure.md) | molecule | Available | [HTML `<details>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element), [APG Disclosure pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/) |
| [Menu button](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md) | molecule | Available | [APG Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/) |
| [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md) | molecule | Available | **Our choice:** No native element or APG pattern exists; a labelled `<nav>` with a list of links and `aria-current="page"` on the current one, as for breadcrumbs. |
| [Popover](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.md) | molecule | Available | [HTML `popover` attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#the-popover-attribute), [MDN Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API) |
| [Search](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.md) | molecule | Available | [HTML `<search>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-search-element), [MDN `<input type="search">`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/search) |
| [Site navigation](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/nav.md) | organism | Available | [HTML `<nav>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element), [APG Landmark regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/), [APG Disclosure navigation example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/) |
| [Tabs](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md) | molecule | Available | [APG Tabs pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/) |
| [Toolbar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.md) | molecule | Available | [APG Toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/) |
| [Typeahead](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md) | molecule | Coming in M3 | [HTML `<datalist>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-datalist-element), [APG Combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/) |

### M3b: App shell, complex layouts and organisms

| Pattern | Level | Status | Follows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md) | layout | Coming in M3b | **Our choice:** No standard defines an app shell; it is the HTML landmarks `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<aside>` placed with CSS grid, with no wrapper elements of our own. |
| [Compact density](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/density.md) | token | Coming in M3b | **Our choice:** No standard exists for density; one semantic token override that tightens space while targets stay at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels. |
| [Dashboard](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dashboard.md) | layout | Coming in M3b | **Our choice:** No standard exists; a CSS grid of `<section>` elements, each with a heading, that reflows without media queries. |
| [Data table](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.md) | organism | Coming in M3b | [HTML `<table>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#the-table-element), [APG Table pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/) |
| [Filter bar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/filter-bar.md) | organism | Coming in M3b | **Our choice:** No standard exists; a `<form>` inside `<search>` with labelled native controls in a row that wraps, and the result count announced as a status message. |
| [Large forms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/large-forms.md) | organism | Coming in M3b | [HTML `<form>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#the-form-element), [HTML `<fieldset>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-fieldset-element) |
| [List-detail](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.md) | layout | Coming in M3b | **Our choice:** No standard exists; a list of links beside the detail region, placed with CSS grid, where each item is a real link so the browser's history and the URL keep working. |
| [Split](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.md) | layout | Coming in M3b | **Our choice:** No standard exists for a fixed split; two regions placed with CSS grid. A divider users can drag would follow the APG Window Splitter pattern. |

## Alerts

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.html

Messages about status, from notices in the page to live alerts for important, time-sensitive changes.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [APG Alert pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-alert="info | success | warning | danger"   an inline alert with a tone
data-alert="toasts"                               the toast region (fixed position)
data-alert="dismiss"                              a toast's dismiss button
role="status" | role="alert"                      native ARIA live regions
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/alerts.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/alerts.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/alerts.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Inline alerts

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div data-alert="info">
    <p><strong>Info:</strong> Maintenance is planned for Sunday at 02:00.</p>
  </div>
  <div data-alert="success">
    <p><strong>Success:</strong> Your changes were published.</p>
  </div>
  <div data-alert="warning">
    <p><strong>Warning:</strong> Your trial ends in 3 days.</p>
    <p><a href="#inline-title">Choose a plan</a> to keep your projects.</p>
  </div>
  <div data-alert="danger">
    <p><strong>Error:</strong> The file could not be uploaded. Try a file under 10 MB.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Live regions

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-announce="live-status">Save settings</button>
  <button type="button" data-announce="live-alert">Send without a subject</button>
</div>
<div id="live-status" role="status"></div>
<div id="live-alert" role="alert"></div>
```

#### Toasts

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <button type="button" data-toast="success">Copy link</button>
  <button type="button" data-toast="info">Start export</button>
  <button type="button" data-toast="danger">Sync now</button>
</div>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/alerts.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/alerts.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | reaches each toast's Dismiss button; toasts never take focus |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on Dismiss, removes the toast and focuses the next one |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: Messages about the state of the page: an inline alert with a tone (info, success, warning, danger), live regions that announce new messages to screen readers, and a toast region that stacks short messages at the bottom inline-end corner of the viewport. <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/status_role> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role> WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html> Live regions: a message that appears without a page load must be announced without moving focus (WCAG 4.1.3). The region MUST be in the page before the message is inserted: screen readers watch regions that exist, so inserting an element that already holds role and text is often not announced. Static alerts that are present on load need no role; they are read with the page. <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA22> <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA19> Tone is never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the message starts with a word ("Warning:") written in the markup, so every user and screen reader gets it, and a decorative icon (CSS generated content with empty alternative text) adds a shape.

### Specs

- **APG Alert pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alert/)
- **WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
- **MDN `status` role**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/status_role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/status_role)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/alert_role)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA22](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA22)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA19](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/aria/ARIA19)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable.html)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/alerts.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/alerts.css)
- [`examples/molecules/alerts.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/alerts.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/alerts.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/alerts.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Feedback](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Note](https://vercel.com/geist/note)

## Breadcrumb

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.html

The path to the current page as an ordered list of links in a labelled `<nav>`.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [APG Breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-breadcrumb       on <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
aria-current="page"   on the last link (native ARIA)
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/breadcrumb.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/breadcrumb.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/breadcrumb.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Breadcrumb

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb" data-breadcrumb>
  <ol>
    <li><a href="../base.html">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="index.html">Molecules</a></li>
    <li><a href="breadcrumb.html" aria-current="page">Breadcrumb</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

#### A long trail wraps

```html
<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb for the archive" data-breadcrumb>
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Documentation</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Components and patterns</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Navigation</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title">Archive</a></li>
    <li><a href="#long-title" aria-current="page">Breadcrumbs in older releases</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

### Keyboard

No keyboard notes yet. Follow the keyboard interaction section of the [APG Breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/).

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: The trail of pages leading to the current one: a \<nav> named "Breadcrumb", an ordered list of links, and aria-current="page" on the last one, as in the APG Breadcrumb pattern. APG: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/> <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element>

### Specs

- **APG Breadcrumb pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/)
- **HTML `<nav>` element**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
- **MDN `aria-current`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/content#alternative_text](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/content#alternative_text)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/breadcrumb.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/breadcrumb.css)
- [`examples/molecules/breadcrumb.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/breadcrumb.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/breadcrumb.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/breadcrumb.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Path controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/path-controls)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Breadcrumbs](https://vercel.com/geist/breadcrumbs)

## Card

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.html

A self-contained item, such as a product or an article teaser, on a raised surface.

**Our choice:** No native element or APG pattern exists; an `<article>` with a heading, where the heading holds the one link, so the whole card is not one long link name.

### Standard

No native element or WAI-ARIA APG pattern covers this.

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-card          on <article> (or <section>, <li>): the card
data-card="link"   the whole card follows the link in its heading
Children: an optional first <img> (or <picture>, <video>) as media,
a heading, body content, and an optional <footer> for actions.
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/card.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/card.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/card.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Atoms

```html
<div class="grid" style="--grid-min: 16rem">
  <article data-card>
    <h3>Starter plan</h3>
    <p>For one person trying things out.</p>
    <p data-text="small muted">Free forever.</p>
    <footer>
      <a href="#grid-title" data-button="primary small">Choose Starter</a>
    </footer>
  </article>
  <article data-card="link">
    <img src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 160'%3E%3Crect width='320' height='160' fill='%233451d1'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='250' cy='40' r='60' fill='%238ea2ff'/%3E%3Crect x='24' y='96' width='140' height='40' rx='8' fill='%23f6f7f9'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="" width="320" height="160">
    <h3><a href="../theming.html">Theming guide</a></h3>
    <p>Override semantic tokens to make a theme, with no build step.</p>
    <footer>
      <span data-badge="accent">Guide</span>
      <a href="../../css/tokens/semantic.css" data-button="secondary small">View tokens</a>
    </footer>
  </article>
  <article data-card="link">
    <img src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 320 160'%3E%3Crect width='320' height='160' fill='%2317773a'/%3E%3Cpath d='M0 160 L120 50 L200 120 L260 70 L320 120 V160Z' fill='%235fd38d'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="" width="320" height="160">
    <h3><a href="../atoms/index.html">Atoms</a></h3>
    <p>Buttons, switches, fields and badges.</p>
  </article>
</div>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/card.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/card.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to each card's heading link, then to its footer actions |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | follows the focused link |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: HTML has no card element and the APG has no card pattern, so the contract is written up in explainers/card.md. <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-article-element>

### Specs

- **HTML `<article>` element**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-article-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-article-element)
- **Other**: [inclusive-components.design/cards/](https://inclusive-components.design/cards/)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html)
- **W3C**: [www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/card.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/card.css)
- [`examples/molecules/card.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/card.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/card.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/card.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- [Material Design 3: Cards](https://m3.material.io/components/cards/overview)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Dialog and drawer

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.html

A modal `<dialog>`, either centered or as a drawer along one edge of the viewport.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [HTML `<dialog>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element)
- [APG Dialog (Modal) pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)

Level: organism. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-dialog                         on <dialog>: header, body and footer layout
                                    and the open transition
data-dialog="drawer [start | end]"  a drawer at the inline-start or inline-end
                                    edge (end is the default)
closedby="any | closerequest | none"  native: how the dialog can be dismissed
Children: an optional <header> (heading and close button) and <footer>
(actions, end-aligned); everything else is the body.
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/dialog.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/dialog.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/dialog.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Delete project?

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="confirm-dialog" command="show-modal">Delete project…</button>
<dialog id="confirm-dialog" data-dialog aria-labelledby="confirm-dialog-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="confirm-dialog-title">Delete project?</h2>
  </header>
  <p>This deletes the project and its 12 files for everyone. You cannot undo it.</p>
  <form method="dialog">
    <footer>
      <button type="submit" value="cancel" data-button="secondary" autofocus>Cancel</button>
      <button type="submit" value="delete">Delete project</button>
    </footer>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

#### Filters

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="filters-drawer" command="show-modal">Filters</button>
<dialog id="filters-drawer" data-dialog="drawer end" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="filters-drawer-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="filters-drawer-title">Filters</h2>
    <button type="button" commandfor="filters-drawer" command="close" data-button="quiet small">Close</button>
  </header>
  <form method="dialog" class="stack">
    <fieldset>
      <legend>Status</legend>
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="show-open" checked> Open</label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="show-closed"> Closed</label>
    </fieldset>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="filters-owner">Owner</label>
      <input id="filters-owner" name="owner" type="text" autocomplete="off">
    </div>
    <footer>
      <button type="submit" value="apply">Apply filters</button>
    </footer>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

#### Menu

```html
<button type="button" commandfor="menu-drawer" command="show-modal">Menu</button>
<dialog id="menu-drawer" data-dialog="drawer start" closedby="any" aria-labelledby="menu-drawer-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="menu-drawer-title">Menu</h2>
    <button type="button" commandfor="menu-drawer" command="close" data-button="quiet small">Close</button>
  </header>
  <nav aria-label="Drawer" data-nav>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#menu-drawer-title" aria-current="page">Overview</a></li>
      <li><a href="#drawer-start-title">Projects</a></li>
      <li><a href="#drawer-start-title">Settings</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
</dialog>
```

#### Autosave is on

```html
<button type="button" data-show-dialog="note-dialog">Show a note</button>
<dialog id="note-dialog" data-dialog closedby="closerequest" aria-labelledby="note-dialog-title">
  <header>
    <h2 id="note-dialog-title">Autosave is on</h2>
    <button type="button" commandfor="note-dialog" command="close" data-button="quiet small">Close</button>
  </header>
  <p>Changes are saved as you type.</p>
</dialog>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/dialog.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/dialog.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on an opener, opens the dialog and moves focus into it |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next focusable element inside the dialog / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | closes the dialog and returns focus to the opener |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: The browser makes the rest of the page inert, moves focus into the dialog, and returns focus to the invoker when it closes. <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API>

### Specs

- **HTML `<dialog>` element**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element)
- **APG Dialog (Modal) pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
- **MDN `<dialog>`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog#closedby](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/dialog#closedby)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@starting-style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@starting-style)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/transition-behavior](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/transition-behavior)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap.html)

## Disclosure

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/disclosure.html

A summary that shows or hides more content, built on `<details>` and `<summary>`.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [HTML `<details>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element)
- [APG Disclosure pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-disclosure="accordion"   on a wrapper around several <details>:
                              joins them into one bordered block
data-disclosure="plain"       on a <details>: no box, for "Show more"
                              text inside prose
name="group"                  on each <details> (native): only one open
open                          on a <details> (native): open on load
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/disclosure.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/disclosure.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/disclosure.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Disclosure

```html
<details>
  <summary>What is included in the plan?</summary>
  <p>Unlimited projects, five collaborators and email support.</p>
</details>
```

#### Exclusive accordion

```html
<div data-disclosure="accordion">
  <details name="faq" open>
    <summary>Shipping</summary>
    <p>Orders ship within two working days.</p>
  </details>
  <details name="faq">
    <summary>Returns</summary>
    <p>Return unused items within 30 days for a full refund.</p>
  </details>
  <details name="faq">
    <summary>Warranty</summary>
    <p>Every product has a two-year warranty.</p>
  </details>
</div>
```

#### Accordion with several open

```html
<div data-disclosure="accordion">
  <details>
    <summary>Monthly plan</summary>
    <p>Pay each month and cancel any time.</p>
  </details>
  <details>
    <summary>Yearly plan</summary>
    <p>Pay once a year and get two months free.</p>
  </details>
</div>
```

#### Inline show more

```html
<p>The release adds pagination, tabs and toasts.</p>
<details data-disclosure="plain">
  <summary>Show the full list of changes</summary>
  <ul>
    <li>Twelve molecules with example pages.</li>
    <li>Five small web components.</li>
    <li>Four explainers for custom patterns.</li>
  </ul>
</details>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/disclosure.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/disclosure.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next summary / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | opens or closes the focused section |

### Specs

- **HTML `<details>` element**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element)
- **APG Disclosure pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details)
- **W3C**: [www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-summary](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aam-1.0/#el-summary)
- **APG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#name](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/details#name)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/disclosure.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/disclosure.css)
- [`examples/molecules/disclosure.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/disclosure.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/disclosure.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/disclosure.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Disclosure controls](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/disclosure-controls)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Collapse](https://vercel.com/geist/collapse)

## Menu button

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.html

A button that opens a menu of actions.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [APG Menu Button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
<dui-menu>                         wraps the button and its popover
popovertarget="menu-id"            on the <button> (native)
popover data-popover               on the menu element
<button> or <a href> children      the actions; <hr> separates groups
Added by the component: aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, role="menu",
role="menuitem", tabindex="-1".
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/menu-button.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/menu-button.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/menu-button.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Actions menu

```html
<dui-menu>
  <button type="button" popovertarget="row-actions">Actions</button>
  <div id="row-actions" popover data-popover>
    <button type="button">Edit</button>
    <button type="button">Duplicate</button>
    <button type="button">Archive</button>
    <hr>
    <button type="button">Delete</button>
  </div>
</dui-menu>
<p role="status" id="menu-result"></p>
```

#### Links are not a menu

```html
<button type="button" popovertarget="account-links">Account</button>
<div id="account-links" popover data-popover>
  <nav aria-label="Account" data-nav>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#links-title">Profile</a></li>
      <li><a href="#links-title">Billing</a></li>
      <li><a href="#links-title">Sign out</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
</div>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/menu-button.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/menu-button.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> / <kbd>Down Arrow</kbd> | on the button, opens the menu and focuses the first item |
| <kbd>Up Arrow</kbd> | on the button, opens the menu and focuses the last item |
| <kbd>Down Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Up Arrow</kbd> | next or previous item, wrapping |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | first or last item |
| <kbd>A letter</kbd> | next item whose label starts with it |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | activates the item and closes the menu |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | closes the menu and returns focus to the button |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | closes the menu and moves on |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: A button that opens a list of actions, following the APG Menu Button pattern: aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded on the button, role="menu" on the list and role="menuitem" on each action. The list is a popover opened with popovertarget, so the browser handles the top layer, light dismiss and Esc; the \<dui-menu> web component (web-components/dui-menu.js) adds the roles and the APG keyboard behavior that HTML has no element for. APG: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/> APG Menu: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/menu_role> When not to use it: if the items are links to other pages, use a disclosure (a \<details> or a popover of links, see nav.css and popover.css) instead. role="menu" tells screen readers to expect an application menu, with arrow-key navigation and no Tab stops, which is wrong for site navigation (see the note in <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/>). Items are at least --dui-size-target tall (WCAG 2.5.8) and show the base focus outline (WCAG 2.4.7).

### Specs

- **APG Menu Button pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)
- **APG Menu and Menubar pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/menu_role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/menu_role)
- **APG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-haspopup](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-haspopup)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/menu-button.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/menu-button.css)
- [`examples/molecules/menu-button.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/menu-button.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/menu-button.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/menu-button.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Pull-down buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/pull-down-buttons)
- [Material Design 3: Menus](https://m3.material.io/components/menus/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Menu](https://vercel.com/geist/menu)

## Pagination

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.html

Links to the pages of a long list of results.

**Our choice:** No native element or APG pattern exists; a labelled `<nav>` with a list of links and `aria-current="page"` on the current one, as for breadcrumbs.

### Standard

No native element or WAI-ARIA APG pattern covers this.

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-pagination        on <nav aria-label="Pagination">
aria-current="page"    on the current page link (native ARIA)
<a> without href       a disabled Previous or Next (native placeholder link)
<li aria-hidden="true">…</li>   a gap in the page numbers
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/pagination.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/pagination.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/pagination.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Middle of a long list

```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination" data-pagination>
  <ul>
    <li><a href="?page=4" rel="prev">Previous<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>1</a></li>
    <li aria-hidden="true">…</li>
    <li><a href="?page=4"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>4</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=5" aria-current="page"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>5</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=6"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>6</a></li>
    <li aria-hidden="true">…</li>
    <li><a href="?page=10"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>10</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=6" rel="next">Next<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

#### First page

```html
<nav aria-label="Pagination, search results" data-pagination>
  <ul>
    <li><a>Previous<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1" aria-current="page"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>1</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=2"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>2</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=3"><span class="visually-hidden">Page </span>3</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=2" rel="next">Next<span class="visually-hidden"> page</span></a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/pagination.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/pagination.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next page link / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | follows the focused link |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: Links between the pages of a long list or search result: a \<nav> named "Pagination" with a list of links, aria-current="page" on the current page, and Previous and Next links. There is no native element and no APG pattern for pagination, so this is a styling contract written up as an explainer: explainers/pagination.md. <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current>

### Specs

- **HTML `<nav>` element**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
- **MDN `aria-current`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-next](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-next)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#the-a-element)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/pagination.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/pagination.css)
- [`examples/molecules/pagination.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/pagination.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/pagination.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/pagination.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Pagination](https://vercel.com/geist/pagination)

## Popover

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.html

Content shown on top of the page from a button, with the `popover` attribute.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [HTML `popover` attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#the-popover-attribute)
- [MDN Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-popover                    on a [popover] element: panel look, anchored
                                below the invoker, aligned to its start edge
data-popover="block-start | inline-start | inline-end"
                                place it above or beside the invoker instead
role="tooltip"                  on a [popover] element: tooltip look,
                                placed above the trigger
popover="auto | manual | hint"  native: auto light-dismisses, manual does not
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/popover.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/popover.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/popover.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Popover

```html
<button type="button" popovertarget="share-popover">Share</button>
<div id="share-popover" popover data-popover>
  <p>Anyone with the link can view this page.</p>
</div>
```

#### Above the button, with a close button

```html
<button type="button" popovertarget="help-popover">Help</button>
<div id="help-popover" popover="manual" data-popover="block-start">
  <p><strong>Need a hand?</strong></p>
  <p>Read the <a href="../../README.md">guide</a> or ask in the forum.</p>
  <button type="button" popovertarget="help-popover" popovertargetaction="hide" data-button="small">Close</button>
</div>
```

#### Tooltip

```html
<div class="cluster">
  <dui-tooltip>
    <button type="button" aria-describedby="save-tip">Save</button>
    <span id="save-tip" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Shortcut: Ctrl+S</span>
  </dui-tooltip>
  <dui-tooltip>
    <button type="button" aria-label="Copy link" aria-describedby="copy-tip" data-button="quiet">⧉</button>
    <span id="copy-tip" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Copies the page address</span>
  </dui-tooltip>
</div>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/popover.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/popover.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on a popover button, opens or closes the popover |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves into the open popover, then on through the page |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | closes an auto popover and returns focus to its button |
| <kbd>Tab to a tooltip trigger</kbd> | shows its tooltip / Esc: hides it, focus stays |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: A button with popovertarget="id" opens and closes the popover with no script; the browser puts it in the top layer, exposes the button's expanded state, and (for popover="auto") closes it on Esc or a click outside ("light dismiss") and returns focus to the button. <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/popover> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API> \<dui-tooltip> \<button type="button" aria-describedby="save-tip">Save\</button> \<span id="save-tip" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Shortcut: Ctrl+S\</span> \</dui-tooltip>

### Specs

- **HTML `popover` attribute**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#the-popover-attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#the-popover-attribute)
- **MDN Popover API**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/popover](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/popover)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_anchor_positioning](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_anchor_positioning)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position-area](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position-area)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position-try-fallbacks](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/position-try-fallbacks)
- **W3C**: [drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/)
- **APG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html)
- **Other**: [open-ui.org/components/interest-invokers.explainer/](https://open-ui.org/components/interest-invokers.explainer/)
