## Search

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.html

A search form in a `<search>` landmark with an `<input type="search">`.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [HTML `<search>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-search-element)
- [MDN `<input type="search">`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/search)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
<search> > <form> with an <input type="search">   no attribute needed:
the label and any hint span the full width, the input and the submit
button share the row below.
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/search.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/search.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/search.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### With a visible label

```html
<search aria-label="Guides">
  <form action="search.html" method="get">
    <label for="guide-search">Search the guides</label>
    <input id="guide-search" type="search" name="q" autocomplete="off" aria-describedby="guide-search-hint">
    <button type="submit">Search</button>
    <p id="guide-search-hint" data-field="hint">Try "tokens" or "dialog".</p>
  </form>
</search>
```

#### Compact, label visually hidden

```html
<search aria-label="Site">
  <form action="search.html" method="get">
    <label for="site-search" class="visually-hidden">Search this site</label>
    <input id="site-search" type="search" name="q" autocomplete="off">
    <button type="submit" data-button="secondary">Search</button>
  </form>
</search>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/search.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/search.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | in the field, submits the search |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | in the field, clears it (in browsers that support it) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves from the field to the button |

### Specs

- **HTML `<search>` element**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-search-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#the-search-element)
- **MDN `<input type="search">`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/search](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/input/search)
- **MDN `<search>`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/search](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/search)
- **W3C**: [www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/labels/)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/search.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/search.css)
- [`examples/molecules/search.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/search.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/search.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/search.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Search fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/search-fields)
- [Material Design 3: Search](https://m3.material.io/components/search/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Search Input](https://vercel.com/geist/search-input)

## Site navigation

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/nav.html

The main links of a site in a `<nav>` landmark, with the current page marked.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [HTML `<nav>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
- [APG Landmark regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/)
- [APG Disclosure navigation example](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/)

Level: organism. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
data-nav="vertical | horizontal"   on <nav> (empty means vertical)
aria-current="page"                on the current link (native ARIA)
<details> / <summary>              inside an <li> for a collapsible group;
                                   open to expand it on load, name for
                                   one-at-a-time
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/nav.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/nav.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/nav.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Vertical (sidebar)

```html
<nav aria-label="Sidebar example" data-nav="vertical">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#vertical-title">Overview</a></li>
    <li>
      <details open>
        <summary>Projects</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title" aria-current="page">Active</a></li>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title">Archived</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
    <li>
      <details>
        <summary>Settings</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title">Profile</a></li>
          <li><a href="#vertical-title">Billing</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

#### Horizontal (top bar)

```html
<nav aria-label="Top bar example" data-nav="horizontal">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#horizontal-title" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
    <li>
      <details name="top-bar">
        <summary>Products</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Design system</a></li>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Icons</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
    <li>
      <details name="top-bar">
        <summary>Company</summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">About</a></li>
          <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Careers</a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
    <li><a href="#horizontal-title">Contact</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/nav.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/nav.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves to the next link or group summary / Shift+Tab: previous |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | on a summary, opens or closes the group |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | on a link, follows it |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: Site or section navigation: a \<nav> landmark with an accessible name, a list of links, aria-current="page" on the link to the current page, and optional collapsible groups made with \<details> and \<summary>.

### Specs

- **HTML `<nav>` element**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element)
- **APG Landmark regions**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/)
- **APG Disclosure navigation example**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/)
- **MDN `aria-current`**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-current)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/nav](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/nav)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F73](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F73)
- **WHATWG**: [html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/nav.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/nav.css)
- [`examples/molecules/nav.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/nav.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/nav.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/nav.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Tabs

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.html

Sections of content shown one at a time, chosen from a list of tabs.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [APG Tabs pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
<dui-tabs>                 wraps a <nav aria-label> with a list of
                           <a href="#panel-id"> links, then the panels
activation="manual"        on <dui-tabs>: arrows move focus, Enter or
                           Space selects (default: automatic)
aria-current="true"        on a link: the tab selected on load (else the
                           tab named in the URL fragment, else the first).
                           The component swaps it for aria-selected;
                           aria-selected is not allowed on a link.
role="tablist" | "tab" | "tabpanel" (added by the component; styled here)
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/tabs.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/tabs.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/tabs.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Notifications

```html
<dui-tabs>
  <nav aria-label="Account settings">
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#tab-profile">Profile</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-security">Security</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-notifications">Notifications</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
  <section id="tab-profile">
    <h3>Profile</h3>
    <p>Your name and photo appear on comments and shared projects.</p>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-security">
    <h3>Security</h3>
    <div data-field>
      <label for="tab-security-code">Recovery code</label>
      <input id="tab-security-code" name="recovery" type="text" autocomplete="off">
    </div>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-notifications">
    <h3>Notifications</h3>
    <p>Email alerts are on. You get a weekly digest on Mondays.</p>
  </section>
</dui-tabs>
```

#### Year

```html
<dui-tabs activation="manual">
  <nav aria-label="Report period">
    <ul>
      <li><a href="#tab-week">Week</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-month" aria-current="true">Month</a></li>
      <li><a href="#tab-year">Year</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
  <section id="tab-week">
    <h3>Week</h3>
    <p>42 orders this week.</p>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-month">
    <h3>Month</h3>
    <p>180 orders this month.</p>
  </section>
  <section id="tab-year">
    <h3>Year</h3>
    <p>2,140 orders this year.</p>
  </section>
</dui-tabs>
```

#### مساعدة

```html
<div dir="rtl" lang="ar">
  <dui-tabs>
    <nav aria-label="الإعدادات">
      <ul>
        <li><a href="#tab-rtl-general">عام</a></li>
        <li><a href="#tab-rtl-privacy">الخصوصية</a></li>
        <li><a href="#tab-rtl-help">مساعدة</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
    <section id="tab-rtl-general">
      <h3>عام</h3>
      <p>الإعدادات العامة للحساب.</p>
    </section>
    <section id="tab-rtl-privacy">
      <h3>الخصوصية</h3>
      <p>من يمكنه رؤية ملفك الشخصي.</p>
    </section>
    <section id="tab-rtl-help">
      <h3>مساعدة</h3>
      <p>الأسئلة الشائعة والدعم.</p>
    </section>
  </dui-tabs>
</div>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/tabs.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/tabs.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves into the tab list (to the selected tab), then to the panel |
| <kbd>Right Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Left Arrow</kbd> | next or previous tab, wrapping (swapped in right-to-left) |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | first or last tab |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | selects the focused tab (manual activation) |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: Layered sections of content where one panel shows at a time, following the APG Tabs pattern (role="tablist", "tab" and "tabpanel", aria-selected, aria-controls, roving tabindex). APG: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/tab_role> The styles target the ARIA roles, so they also fit tabs rendered by a framework that follows the APG with its own script.

### Specs

- **APG Tabs pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/tab_role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/tab_role)
- **APG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/#deciding-when-to-make-selection-automatically-follow-focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/#deciding-when-to-make-selection-automatically-follow-focus)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/tabpanel_role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/tabpanel_role)
- **W3C**: [www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-nav](https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/#el-nav)
- **WCAG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/tabs.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/tabs.css)
- [`examples/molecules/tabs.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/tabs.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/tabs.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/tabs.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Tab views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-views)
- [Material Design 3: Tabs](https://m3.material.io/components/tabs/overview)
- [Vercel Geist: Tabs](https://vercel.com/geist/tabs)

## Toolbar

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.html

A row of related controls that is one stop in the tab order.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [APG Toolbar pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### API

```text
role="toolbar" aria-label="…"     on the container (<dui-toolbar> or any element)
aria-orientation="vertical"       optional; default horizontal
aria-pressed="true | false"       on toggle buttons (native ARIA)
<hr>                              a separator between groups of controls
```

### Live example

- [Open the example on its own](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/molecules/toolbar.html)

### Markup

The `<pre><code>` blocks in [`examples/molecules/toolbar.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/toolbar.html), HTML-unescaped and otherwise unchanged, each named by the heading of its section:

#### Text formatting

```html
<dui-toolbar role="toolbar" aria-label="Text formatting">
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">Bold</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Italic</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Underline</button>
  <hr>
  <button type="button">Insert link</button>
  <button type="button">Clear formatting</button>
</dui-toolbar>
```

#### Vertical

```html
<dui-toolbar role="toolbar" aria-label="Drawing tools" aria-orientation="vertical">
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">Select</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Pen</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Eraser</button>
</dui-toolbar>
```

### Keyboard

From the `Keyboard` block in [`examples/molecules/toolbar.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/toolbar.html).

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | moves into the toolbar (to the last focused control), then out of it |
| <kbd>Right Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Left Arrow</kbd> | next or previous control, wrapping (swapped in right-to-left) |
| <kbd>Down Arrow</kbd> / <kbd>Up Arrow</kbd> | the same in a vertical toolbar |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> / <kbd>End</kbd> | first or last control |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Space</kbd> | activates the focused button |

### Accessibility

From the CSS header comment: A labelled row (or column) of controls, such as text formatting buttons, following the APG Toolbar pattern: role="toolbar" with aria-label, one Tab stop for the whole group, and arrow keys between the controls (roving tabindex). HTML has no toolbar element and cannot do roving focus, so the \<dui-toolbar> web component (web-components/dui-toolbar.js) adds the keyboard behavior. APG: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/> <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/toolbar_role>

### Specs

- **APG Toolbar pattern**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/toolbar_role](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/toolbar_role)
- **MDN**: [developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-pressed](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-pressed)
- **APG**: [www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex)

### Source

- [`css/components/molecules/toolbar.css`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/molecules/toolbar.css)
- [`examples/molecules/toolbar.html`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/examples/molecules/toolbar.html)
- [`site/content/patterns/toolbar.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/site/content/patterns/toolbar.md)

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Toolbars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/toolbars)
- [Material Design 3: Toolbars](https://m3.material.io/components/toolbars/overview)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Typeahead

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.html

A text field that suggests values as you type, with `<datalist>` first and an APG combobox only where `<datalist>` falls short.

Coming in M3.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [HTML `<datalist>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-datalist-element)
- [APG Combobox pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/)

Level: molecule. Milestone: M3: Molecules and navigation patterns.

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Combo boxes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/combo-boxes)
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Combobox](https://vercel.com/geist/combobox)

## App shell

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.html

The frame of an application: header, primary sidebar, main content and an optional auxiliary sidebar.

**Our choice:** No standard defines an app shell; it is the HTML landmarks `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<aside>` placed with CSS grid, with no wrapper elements of our own.

Coming in M3b.

### Standard

No native element or WAI-ARIA APG pattern covers this.

Level: layout. Milestone: M3b: App shell, complex layouts and organisms.

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- [Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Sidebars](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sidebars)
- [Material Design 3: Scaffold](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/scaffold/overview)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Compact density

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/density.html

A compact density token that tightens spacing for data-heavy screens.

**Our choice:** No standard exists for density; one semantic token override that tightens space while targets stay at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels.

Coming in M3b.

### Standard

No native element or WAI-ARIA APG pattern covers this.

Level: token. Milestone: M3b: App shell, complex layouts and organisms.

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- [Material Design 3: Grids & spacing: Density](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/grids-spacing/density)
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Dashboard

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dashboard.html

A grid of summary sections, each with a heading, that reflows to fit the screen.

**Our choice:** No standard exists; a CSS grid of `<section>` elements, each with a heading, that reflows without media queries.

Coming in M3b.

### Standard

No native element or WAI-ARIA APG pattern covers this.

Level: layout. Milestone: M3b: App shell, complex layouts and organisms.

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Apple Human Interface Guidelines: No equivalent
- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- Vercel Geist: No equivalent

## Data table

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.html

Rows of records in a native `<table>` with a caption, header cells and optional sorting.

Coming in M3b.

### Standard

This pattern follows:

- [HTML `<table>` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#the-table-element)
- [APG Table pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/table/)

Level: organism. Milestone: M3b: App shell, complex layouts and organisms.

### How other systems do it

For comparison only; these are not the standard this system follows.

- Material Design 3: No equivalent
- [Vercel Geist: Table](https://vercel.com/geist/table)

## Filter bar

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/filter-bar.html

A row of native form controls that narrows a list or table.

**Our choice:** No standard exists; a `<form>` inside `<search>` with labelled native controls in a row that wraps, and the result count announced as a status message.

Coming in M3b.

### Standard

## List-detail

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.html

A list of items beside the details of the selected one, stacked on narrow screens.

**Our choice:** No standard exists; a list of links beside the detail region, placed with CSS grid, where each item is a real link so the browser's history and the URL keep working.

## Split

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.html

Two regions side by side at a set ratio, stacked on narrow screens.

**Our choice:** No standard exists for a fixed split; two regions placed with CSS grid. A divider users can drag would follow the APG Window Splitter pattern.

Coming in M3b.

## Guides

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/index.html

- [From a simple site to an ERP app](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/simple-site-to-erp-app.md): Five steps from a plain content page to a dense business application, and which parts of each step are available today.

## From a simple site to an ERP app

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/guides/simple-site-to-erp-app.html

Each step adds to the one before it, so a site can stop at any step. The lists below come from the [pattern registry](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/index.md) and show each pattern's status as of this build.

### Step 1: a plain content page

Write semantic HTML and link `css/domestic.css`. Headings, paragraphs, lists, links, tables, forms and `<dialog>` get their look from the base layer with no classes; see [Base elements](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/components/base.md). Arrange content with the layout primitives:

- [Cluster](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/cluster.md): An inline group that wraps onto new lines (buttons, tags, nav links).
- [Grid](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/grid.md): A responsive grid: as many columns as fit, each at least --grid-min wide, never wider than the container.
- [Scroll](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/scroll.md): A scroll container for content wider than the screen (data tables, long code, wide media), so it scrolls on its own instead of widening the page (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow allows two-dimensional scrolling for data tables: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html>).
- [Stack](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/layouts/stack.md): Vertical flow with a consistent gap between children.

Theme by overriding semantic tokens; see [Tokens](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/tokens/index.md) and the [theming example](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/theming.html).

### Step 2: site navigation

Add the main navigation, a breadcrumb trail and a search form:

- [Site navigation](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/nav.md): The main links of a site in a `<nav>` landmark, with the current page marked. Available.
- [Breadcrumb](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/breadcrumb.md): The path to the current page as an ordered list of links in a labelled `<nav>`. Available.
- [Search](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/search.md): A search form in a `<search>` landmark with an `<input type="search">`. Available.
- [Pagination](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/pagination.md): Links to the pages of a long list of results. Available.

All of these are available.

### Step 3: interactive widgets

Use a native element where one exists (`<details>`, `<dialog>`, `popover`, `<datalist>`), and an APG pattern where one does not:

- [Disclosure](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/disclosure.md): A summary that shows or hides more content, built on `<details>` and `<summary>`. Available.
- [Tabs](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/tabs.md): Sections of content shown one at a time, chosen from a list of tabs. Available.
- [Dialog and drawer](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dialog.md): A modal `<dialog>`, either centered or as a drawer along one edge of the viewport. Available.
- [Popover](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/popover.md): Content shown on top of the page from a button, with the `popover` attribute. Available.
- [Menu button](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/menu-button.md): A button that opens a menu of actions. Available.
- [Toolbar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/toolbar.md): A row of related controls that is one stop in the tab order. Available.
- [Typeahead](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/typeahead.md): A text field that suggests values as you type, with `<datalist>` first and an APG combobox only where `<datalist>` falls short. Coming in M3.
- [Alerts](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/alerts.md): Messages about status, from notices in the page to live alerts for important, time-sensitive changes. Available.
- [Card](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/card.md): A self-contained item, such as a product or an article teaser, on a raised surface. Available.

Not available yet: Typeahead (M3).

### Step 4: the app shell

Frame the application with a primary sidebar for navigation and an auxiliary sidebar for context, then lay out each screen as a list with details, a split view or a dashboard:

- [App shell](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/app-shell.md): The frame of an application: header, primary sidebar, main content and an optional auxiliary sidebar. Coming in M3b.
- [List-detail](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/list-detail.md): A list of items beside the details of the selected one, stacked on narrow screens. Coming in M3b.
- [Split](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/split.md): Two regions side by side at a set ratio, stacked on narrow screens. Coming in M3b.
- [Dashboard](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/dashboard.md): A grid of summary sections, each with a heading, that reflows to fit the screen. Coming in M3b.

None of these are available yet: App shell (M3b), List-detail (M3b), Split (M3b), Dashboard (M3b).

### Step 5: data-heavy screens

Show records in a native `<table>`, narrow them with a filter bar, group long forms with `<fieldset>`, and switch to the compact density token where users scan a lot of data:

- [Data table](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/data-table.md): Rows of records in a native `<table>` with a caption, header cells and optional sorting. Coming in M3b.
- [Filter bar](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/filter-bar.md): A row of native form controls that narrows a list or table. Coming in M3b.
- [Large forms](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/large-forms.md): Long forms split into labelled groups, in one or more columns. Coming in M3b.
- [Compact density](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/patterns/density.md): A compact density token that tightens spacing for data-heavy screens. Coming in M3b.

None of these are available yet: Data table (M3b), Filter bar (M3b), Large forms (M3b), Compact density (M3b).

## Demos

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/demos.html

The same two views, a household-chores **dashboard** and an **account settings** form,
built four ways to show that domestic-ui works with plain HTML and with common frameworks.
Every view uses the same native markup, the `stack`, `cluster` and `grid` layout primitives, and
the [atom APIs](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/css/components/atoms/README.md): `data-text`, `data-button`, `data-field`,
`data-badge` and the `role="switch"` checkbox, written exactly as in
[`examples/atoms/`](https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/examples/atoms/index.html).

Each directory in [`demos/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos) with a `README.md`, by name, with the first sentence of that README. Demos are not part of this site; follow the link to read the source and how to run it.

- **Accessibility checker** ([`demos/a11y/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/a11y)): Checks the built demo apps the same way the repository checks `examples/`: Playwright with [axe](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) (tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`), in light and dark, with every `<details>` opened and checked again.
- **Angular** ([`demos/angular/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/angular)): The dashboard and account settings views in Angular 22: standalone components, two routes (`''` and `'settings'`) with Angular Router, a `title` per route, and `routerLinkActive` with `ariaCurrentWhenActive="page"` for the current link.
- **Astro** ([`demos/astro/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/astro)): The dashboard and account settings views as two static Astro pages (`src/pages/index.astro` and `src/pages/settings.astro`) sharing `src/layouts/Base.astro`.
- **React** ([`demos/react/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/react)): The dashboard and account settings views in React 19 with Vite, as a two-page [multi-page app](https://vite.dev/guide/build#multi-page-app) (`index.html` and `settings.html`).
- **Plain HTML** ([`demos/vanilla/`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/tree/main/demos/vanilla)): The dashboard and account settings views as two static HTML files, with no build step.

## Contributing to domestic-ui

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/contributing.html

Rendered read-only from [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). To change it, [edit CONTRIBUTING.md on GitHub](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/edit/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Thanks for helping. This project is a design system built on native HTML, CSS tokens, and published web standards.

### Issues and pull requests

Use the issue forms for bugs and feature requests. Pull requests should use the template.

Branch names follow `fix/short-description`, `feat/short-description`, `docs/short-description`, or `a11y/short-description`.

#### Approval flow

Issues and pull requests from outside this repository's owners, members, or collaborators get the `needs-owen-approval` label automatically.

The maintainer approves an item by adding the `owen-approved` label. Only Owen applies that label. Team bots never apply `owen-approved` and never merge outside pull requests. Bots may merge their own pull requests.

An outside pull request cannot merge until the `owen-gate` check passes, which requires the `owen-approved` label.

`.github/CODEOWNERS` lists @odonckers on every file. That file is informational today: team bots push with the same GitHub account as Owen, so GitHub cannot tell his review apart from a bot's.

### Standards

- Prefer a native HTML element before adding a component or custom behavior.
- Cite the relevant [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/), [WHATWG](https://whatwg.org/), [W3C](https://www.w3.org/), [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), or [APG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) documentation in the issue or pull request.
- If we choose a behavior the specs leave open, label it as our choice, not as a standard.
- Theme only through semantic `--dui-*` CSS custom properties. Do not hard-code colors, spacing, typography, or other design values in components.

The default theme should look complete and consistent out of the box. Consumers re-theme the system by overriding those tokens.

### Checks

`npm test` must pass. That run includes html-validate, axe, and stylelint.

### Changelog

Every user-facing change needs an entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Changelog

Page: https://odonckers.github.io/domestic-ui/changelog.html

Rendered read-only from [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). To change it, [edit CHANGELOG.md on GitHub](https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/edit/main/CHANGELOG.md).

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
Semantic token names and file paths under `css/` are public API; primitive tokens are not.

### [Unreleased]

#### Added

- `css/domestic.css`: zero-build entry point declaring
  `@layer reset, tokens, base, layout, components, utilities;` and importing each layer file.
- `reset` layer: a modest modern reset (`css/reset/reset.css`).
- `tokens` layer: primitive tokens (`css/tokens/primitives.css`) and semantic tokens
  (`css/tokens/semantic.css`), all prefixed `--dui-`, with `light-dark()` colors,
  a fluid `clamp()` type scale, spacing, radii, focus and motion tokens that collapse
  under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Theme scoping with `[data-theme]` or `.theme-*`, and scheme forcing with
  `data-color-scheme="light" | "dark"`.
- `base` layer: styles for text, links, lists, quotes, code, media, tables, form controls,
  buttons, `<dialog>`, `<details>`, visible `:focus-visible` and forced-colors support.
- `layout` layer: `.stack`, `.cluster` and `.grid` primitives configured with custom properties.
- `utilities` layer: `.visually-hidden`.
- Placeholders for `css/components/` and `web-components/`.
- `examples/base.html` and `examples/theming.html`.
- `PRINCIPLES.md`, including the semantic token reference.
- Tooling: html-validate, Stylelint, a token discipline check, and Playwright + axe-core
  accessibility tests in light and dark, all run by `npm test`.
- GitHub Actions: CI on pull requests and pushes to `main`, and a GitHub Pages skeleton.
- Atoms in `css/components/atoms/`, imported into the `components` layer, each with one attribute API:
  - Text helpers: `data-text="lead | small | muted"`.
  - Quiet link: `data-link="quiet"` (inherits text color, keeps its underline).
  - Buttons: `data-button="[primary | secondary | quiet] [small | large]"` on `<button>`, `<input>`
    and `<a href>`; `aria-disabled="true"` and `aria-busy="true"` states; an inner focus ring on
    primary buttons. `type="submit"` stays primary by default.
  - Switch: `role="switch"` on `<input type="checkbox">`, per the APG Switch pattern, with
    forced-colors support.
  - Field: `data-field` with `data-field="hint"` and `data-field="error"`; invalid style for
    `aria-invalid="true"` and `:user-invalid`.
  - Badge: `data-badge="neutral | accent | success | warning | danger"`.
- Semantic tokens: `--dui-color-warning`, `--dui-color-accent-surface`, `--dui-color-success-surface`,
  `--dui-color-warning-surface`, `--dui-color-danger-surface`, `--dui-tint-amount`, `--dui-border-tint-amount`,
  `--dui-size-target-small`, `--dui-size-target-large` (and their primitives).
- `examples/atoms/`: an index and one page per atom; the theming example now shows atoms in both themes.
- Tests: atom states through Playwright accessibility APIs, rendered focus-ring contrast on every
  button variant, contrast pairs for every new token, and scoped theming of atoms.
- Firefox and WebKit Playwright projects alongside Chromium, installed in CI.
- `layout` layer: `data-scroll="inline"` (`css/layout/scroll.css`), a keyboard-focusable scroll
  container for wide content such as data tables, used on a `<section>` named by the table caption (a region landmark).
- Tests: `tests/mobile.spec.js` checks every example at 320×640 and 375×812 in Chromium, Firefox
  and WebKit for horizontal page overflow and axe violations.
- Molecules in `css/components/molecules/`, imported into the `components` layer after the atoms,
  each documented in its file header (API, example, keyboard, specs) and indexed in
  `css/components/molecules/README.md`:
  - Disclosure and accordion (`disclosure.css`): native `<details>`/`<summary>`, exclusive groups with
    `name`; `data-disclosure="accordion | plain"`.
  - Dialog and drawer (`dialog.css`): header/body/footer layout and open transition for `<dialog>`;
    `data-dialog="drawer [start | end]"`; invoker commands and `closedby`; `@starting-style` with a
    no-transition fallback.
  - Popover and tooltip (`popover.css`): `data-popover="[block-start | inline-start | inline-end]"`,
    anchored with CSS anchor positioning inside `@supports` (bottom-center fallback); tooltips are
    `role="tooltip"` on `popover="hint"`.
  - Navigation list (`nav.css`): `data-nav="vertical | horizontal"`, `aria-current="page"`, `<details>` groups.
  - Breadcrumb (`breadcrumb.css`): `data-breadcrumb`, separators with empty alternative text.
  - Tabs (`tabs.css`): styles for `role="tablist" | "tab" | "tabpanel"`.
  - Menu button (`menu-button.css`): items of a `<dui-menu>` popover.
  - Toolbar (`toolbar.css`): `role="toolbar"`, `aria-orientation`, `aria-pressed` toggles.
  - Pagination (`pagination.css`): `data-pagination`, `aria-current="page"`, placeholder links for disabled ends.
  - Search field (`search.css`): the native `<search>` element around a search form.
  - Card (`card.css`): `data-card` and `data-card="link"` (heading link stretched over the card).
  - Alert and toast (`alerts.css`): `data-alert="info | success | warning | danger"` with a text prefix and
    an icon; `data-alert="toasts"` region; live region guidance.
- Web components in `web-components/`, light DOM, progressive enhancement, no dependencies:
  `<dui-tabs>` (APG Tabs from in-page links and sections; `aria-current="true"` on the link selected on
  load, swapped for `aria-selected` on upgrade; automatic or manual activation; RTL),
  `<dui-menu>` (APG Menu Button keyboard on a popover), `<dui-toolbar>` (roving tabindex),
  `<dui-tooltip>` (show on hover and focus, Esc to hide; stands in for `interestfor`) and
  `<dui-toaster>` (`show()` and `dismiss()` for a toast region, no auto-dismiss).
- Explainers in `explainers/` for the custom patterns: card, pagination, drawer and toast, plus an index.
- Semantic tokens: `--dui-color-info`, `--dui-color-info-surface`, `--dui-color-surface-inverse`,
  `--dui-color-text-inverse`, `--dui-border-width-indicator`, `--dui-size-menu-min`, `--dui-size-drawer`
  (and primitives `--dui-border-3`, `--dui-size-12`, `--dui-size-24`).
- `examples/molecules/`: an index and one page per molecule; the theming example now shows a breadcrumb,
  an alert, tabs and a card in both themes; "Molecules" links in the example navigation.
- Tests (`tests/molecules.spec.js` and additions to the existing specs): APG keyboard behavior for tabs,
  menu button, toolbar, dialog and drawer, popover, tooltip, disclosure and nav groups; ARIA states through
  accessibility APIs; no-JavaScript fallbacks; fallback paths for anchor positioning, `@starting-style`,
  `closedby` and `popover="hint"`; rendered indicator and focus-ring contrast; contrast pairs for every new
  token; scoped theming of molecules. The axe test now also checks open popovers and menus, every tab,
  shown tooltips and toasts, and waits for transitions to finish.
- `PRINCIPLES.md`: molecule choices, new semantic tokens, and "Web components" and "Explainers" sections.

#### Fixed

- Pages no longer scroll sideways on small screens (320px and up). Inline `code`, `kbd`, `samp`
  and links in running text wrap with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, long words in headings break,
  `.cluster` and `.grid` children get `min-inline-size: 0`, badges wrap (a wrapped badge keeps
  rounded corners), table cells use `--dui-space-xs` padding on every side, and every example
  table sits in a `data-scroll="inline"` region. Every example `<pre>` block (in
  `examples/base.html`, `examples/theming.html` and `examples/atoms/`) now has `tabindex="0"`
  and is keyboard-focusable (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`).

- Base button hover and press styles no longer apply to buttons with `aria-disabled="true"`.

[Unreleased]: https://github.com/odonckers/domestic-ui/commits/main
